functions.summary: IPC stub for command 0x001A with no parameters; returns the result or the TLS output word.

functions.name: maybe_Snd_SendIpcStatus
functions.signature: int maybe_Snd_SendIpcStatus(unsigned int* session, unsigned int handle, unsigned int flags, unsigned int* out0, unsigned int* out1)
functions.summary: Status query with header 0x00130042 (command 0x13, one normal and two translated words): stores the handle and flags, sends svc 0x32, and on success writes TLS+0x88 to *out1 and TLS+0x90 to *out0 - note the outputs are swapped relative to the parameter order.

functions.name: Svc_CloseSessionHandles
functions.summary: Closes the GPU session's three handles and its event: sets the 'closing' flag, calls svc 0x18, takes the event lock (svc 0x24), marks the event, signals it via 0x118170, then closes the event and the three handles with svc 0x23.

functions.name: Gfx_IpcCmd4B00C2
functions.signature: int Gfx_IpcCmd4B00C2(u32 handle, u32 buf, int size, u32 arg4, int b, u32* out)
functions.summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x004B (3 normal + 2 translated parameters): sends handle/buf/size/a and the size-packed descriptor, returning the result and the 0x88 output word.

functions.name: Gfx_IpcCmdC0104
functions.signature: u32 Gfx_IpcCmdC0104(u32 handle, u32 buf, u32 size, u32 offset, int count, u32 arg6)
functions.summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x000C (4 normal + 1 translated parameter) used for chunked buffer reads: sends handle/buf/size/offset plus the count descriptor and returns the result.

functions.name: Gfx_IpcCmdF0100
functions.signature: int Gfx_IpcCmdF0100(u8 arg1, u32 b, u8 c, u32 d, u8* out)
functions.summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x000F (4 normal parameters): sends a/b/c/d, and on success writes the 0x88 output byte to *out.

functions.name: Gfx_IpcCmdE0080
functions.signature: int Gfx_IpcCmdE0080(u32* out1, u32 handle, u32* out2, u32 src, int arg5, u32* out3, u32* out4)
functions.summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x000E (2 normal + 2 translated parameters): submits a source/size descriptor and returns four output words (handle, offset, flags, size) to the caller.

functions.name: Gfx_IpcCmdD0080
functions.signature: int Gfx_IpcCmdD0080(u32* out1, u32 handle, u32* out2, u32 src, int arg5, u32* out3, u32* out4)
functions.summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x000D (2 normal + 2 translated parameters): used as the event-wait/transfer request; returns four output words on success.

functions.name: Gfx_IpcCmd400042
functions.summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x0040 (2 translated parameters): sends a and the descriptor b<<14|2 and returns the result or the echoed word.

functions.name: Gfx_IpcCmd3F0040
functions.summary: IPC stub for GPU command 0x003F with one translated parameter; returns the result or the echoed word.

functions.name: Svc_QueryStatus3C
functions.summary: Parameterless IPC query with header 0x3C0000 (command 0x3C) on the fixed session at 0x7B0054; on success writes the reply byte at TLS+0x88 to *out and returns the status word.

functions.name: Os_IpcSendCommand3D
functions.summary: Sends driver command 0x3D with one normal parameter (header 0x003D0040) on the fixed session handle at 0x7B0054 and returns the reply word; a negative Result is returned unchanged.

functions.name: Svc_QueryStatus3B
functions.summary: Parameterless IPC query with header 0x3B0000 (command 0x3B, written as the literal 0x3AFFF4+0xC) on the fixed session at 0x7B0054; writes the reply byte at TLS+0x88 to *out.

functions.name: Os_IpcSendCommand13
functions.summary: Sends driver command 0x13 with one normal parameter (header 0x00130040) on the fixed session handle at 0x7B0054 and returns the reply word.

functions.name: Math_ClampVectorToRing
functions.signature: int Math_ClampVectorToRing(u16* outX, u16* outY, int dx, int dy, int innerRadius, int outerRadius)
functions.summary: Clamps a 2D offset into an annulus: computes length^2 = dx^2+dy^2, returns zero vectors when it is inside the inner radius, otherwise derives the integer square root with a bit-wise loop (0x11CD80 = unsigned division) and writes dx and dy scaled by (limit-inner)*128/sqrt to outX/outY, returning the remaining signed radial distance.

functions.name: Snd_InsertChannelByPriority
functions.summary: Inserts a channel into the mixer's priority-ordered list: builds the channel's list node (func_0011FCBC), computes its priority as volume + pan clamped to 0..0x7F and splices it in before the first channel with a higher value (the comparison flips for tie-breaking depending on the mixer's blend flag), then links it (func_0011FCF8).

functions.name: Snd_ListInsertByPriority
functions.summary: Inserts an entry into the priority-ordered sound list at the first position whose clamped priority is lower (or equal in strict mode) than the new entry's, then links it with 0x11FCF8.

functions.name: Mem_Pool_DestroyAllEntries
functions.summary: Destroys every entry of a small-block pool: walks the intrusive list anchored at pool+4, destroys each element body (node-0x110) with the element destructor 0x123558, unlinks the node with 0x11FCBC and finally releases it with 0x123588. Used when a pool is torn down.

functions.name: Gfx_SetFrameColorParam
functions.signature: void Gfx_SetFrameColorParam(void* self, const u8* arg2)
functions.summary: Sets the frame's colour parameter: calls the device vtable +0x14 with (self->f_10, 2) and copies the two colour bytes into the current frame record at +0x126/+0x12A.

functions.name: maybe_Gfx_CmdList_PushTextureRows
functions.signature: void maybe_Gfx_CmdList_PushTextureRows(u32 cmdWord, u32 count, const u32* src)
functions.summary: Appends raw texture rows to the GPU command list in chunks of at most 0x80 words: writes the header ((n-1)<<20)|0xF0000|cmdWord, copies the pixels (64-byte blocks through 0x0011CD00 where possible) and advances the global write pointer 0x007AED34; on overflow it resets the pointer to the buffer end.

functions.name: maybe_Gfx_CmdList_ResetSlot
functions.summary: Marks a slot free: calls the lock helper 0x12032C, resolves the slot with 0x120368 and stores -1 into the word 0x98 bytes before the returned pointer. 0x120368 itself is `mvn r1,#0; str r1,[r0,#0x1c]; bx lr`, so it takes a pointer and invalidates its +0x1C word.

functions.name: maybe_Pack_ReleaseMemberHandles4
functions.summary: Releases the four generation-tagged handle members at +4, +0xC, +0x14 and +0x1C of the object whose base is self-0x1C, then returns that base. A destructor body for a class with four handle members.

functions.name: maybe_Pack_ReleaseMemberHandles1
functions.summary: Releases the single generation-tagged handle member at +4 of the object whose base is self-4 and returns that base. The one-handle variant of 0x00120408.

functions.name: Pack_LoadMasterTables
functions.summary: Boot-time master-data loader. Resolves every core BXON table from the pack manager by literal name (item, player params for all party members, scenario params, level map/area, region, global flags, save points, sound arcs/groups/BGM/ME/SE, movie list, NG words, panel/panel_line, program_param) and stores the object/handle pairs in the data singleton; the player_param_* group goes through 0x124904 and the scenario_param_* group through 0x1249E0.

functions.name: maybe_Container_MultiList_Init
functions.signature: void maybe_Container_MultiList_Init(Container * c, u32 u32, u32 u322, u32 u323)
functions.summary: Constructor of a container with three intrusive list heads: clears the scalar fields, stores the caller vtable, makes +0x54/+0x58/+0x5C self-referential and default-constructs seven 0x28-byte sub-records at +0x104, forwarding arg4.

functions.name: Os_SvcCallChecked
functions.summary: Checked kernel/IPC call wrapper: runs the command wrapper 0x00117AB8 and, when it fails with anything other than the 'not found' class 0xFFFFFFF9, reports the Result to the SDK error handler 0x0011ED40 with the call-site address 0x001221F4. Returns the Result unchanged.

functions.name: maybe_Svc_Ir_SetupChannel
functions.signature: u32 maybe_Svc_Ir_SetupChannel(u32 service, u32 buffer, int first, u32 width, int c, u32 height, u32 mode)
functions.summary: Opens the shared ir:USER session on first use, maps the shared memory, sends the channel setup request (coordinates and sizes in 8.8 fixed point) and initialises the endpoint, cleaning up on failure.

functions.name: Os_ReadChunkedTable
functions.signature: int Os_ReadChunkedTable(Reader* reader, int* bytesRead, int offset, u32 size)
functions.summary: Reads up to `size` bytes through a reader in at most 0x40-byte requests, adding the wrapped 16-bit current offset each time, and accumulates how many bytes were transferred. It is the small-block reader the parameter-table lookups use.

functions.name: maybe_Os_GetCurrentProcessHandle
functions.summary: Replaces *out with a process handle queried through command 0x0A on the driver session, closing the previous handle with svc 0x23 first and aborting through 0x0011ED40 when the query fails.

functions.name: maybe_Os_PerfSample_Loop
functions.summary: One sampling pass of the SDK timing loop: for each configured entry it reads the system tick, sleeps and accumulates elapsed microseconds against the 1,000,000 constant, stopping early at the 0x3FE marker, then sets the state word at 0x007B00E0 to 3 or 0.

functions.name: maybe_Fs_ReadRecordWithRetry
functions.signature: int maybe_Fs_ReadRecordWithRetry(u32 dst, u32* outLen, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
functions.summary: Drives a stack-allocated provider object (vtable 0x00780FA4) through command 0x45: queries 0x00123BAC, calls the provider's virtual +4, creates a kernel handle, then loops on 0x001228A8 with svcWaitSynchronization1 (0x24) and svcCloseHandle (0x23), retrying up to three times and copying the payload to dst.

functions.name: maybe_Os_SvcCallCheckedAlt
functions.summary: Second checked IPC-send helper: calls one of the two raw send wrappers (Os_IpcSendCommand0D / Os_IpcSendCommand0E, chosen by condition flags the decompiler lost), then applies the same error policy as 0x001221C0 - 0xFFFFFFF9 is ignored, any other negative Result is reported through 0x0011ED40 - and returns the raw result.

functions.name: Svc_Ir_IpcCmd0B0000
functions.summary: Parameterless IPC request with header 0x000B0000 (command 0x0B) on the ir:USER session at 0x007B2D2C; on success it writes the second reply word (TLS+0x8C) to *out and returns the first (TLS+0x84). Dead code: nothing branches to it.

functions.name: Fs_ReadRecordBlock
functions.signature: u32 Fs_ReadRecordBlock(u32 stream, u32 offset, u32* dst, int* read, int updatePosition)
functions.summary: Reads one length-prefixed record from a stream at offset, returns the bytes read and advances the tracked stream position when requested.

functions.name: Mem_AllocAddressRange
functions.signature: unsigned int Mem_AllocAddressRange(MemRange* range, MemRangeNode* node, unsigned int size, unsigned int align)
functions.summary: First-fit allocation inside a linear address range: searches the sorted free-range list for a gap that fits `size+align`, splits it, links the caller's node into the list at the right place and returns the chosen base address.

functions.name: maybe_Os_HandleInit
functions.summary: Creates a kernel handle through 0x0012038C into an empty *out slot and aborts through 0x00118100 on failure; when *out is already non-NULL it deliberately aborts with 0xE0A0183B, so it is a create-once helper.

functions.name: Mem_HeapAllocBlock
functions.signature: unsigned int Mem_HeapAllocBlock(MemHeapState* state, unsigned int size, int align)
functions.summary: Core block allocator: rounds the size to 4 bytes, walks the free list best-fit for the given alignment (two directions), and carves the block through 0x123E6C, which also updates the heap's statistics.

functions.name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelMode
functions.signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelMode(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, int mode, unsigned char priority)
functions.summary: Sets a channel's play mode (byte at +0xE) and, when the mode is 0, its priority (+0x39), then marks the channel block dirty with bit 0x20000. Uses the second channel table (selector +0x131E, pointers at +0x10B4), not the +0x1322/+0x10A4 table the field setters use.

functions.name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelWord34
functions.signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelWord34(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned int value)
functions.summary: Stores a 32-bit word at +0x34 of the channel block and marks it dirty with bit 0x40000. The only caller (0x0011EE78) computes the value before the call, so it is a caller-supplied parameter rather than a fixed constant.

functions.name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelWaveData
functions.signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelWaveData(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned int* data)
functions.summary: Copies 0x20 bytes from the caller's descriptor into the channel's wave slot (table at +0x1234 selected by the +0x1322 double-buffer index) and sets dirty bit 4.

functions.name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelWord3A
functions.signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelWord3A(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned short value)
functions.summary: Stores a 16-bit value at +0x3A of the channel block and marks it dirty with bit 0x400000.

functions.name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelLoopPoints
functions.signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelLoopPoints(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned short start, unsigned short end)
functions.summary: Writes a byte at +0xF and a halfword at +0x3E of the channel block and marks it dirty with bit 0x800000.

functions.name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelAdpcmParams
functions.signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelAdpcmParams(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned short arg3, unsigned short b, unsigned short c, unsigned short d, unsigned short e)
functions.summary: Writes five consecutive fields of the channel block (+0x40, +0x42, +0x44, +0x46 and the byte at +0x45) and marks it dirty with bit 0x1000000.

functions.name: Snd_SetChannelMatrix
functions.summary: Scales the twelve coefficients at +0x0E..+0x19 of the caller's channel state by the scalar at +0x1A and hands the 3x4 result to the matrix writer 0x124050.

functions.name: maybe_Os_ReleaseSharedHandle
functions.summary: Releases one reference to the shared kernel handle at 0x007AF900: when the refcount at 0x007AF8F8+4 drops below 2 it closes the handle with svcCloseHandle, decrements the count and restores the process-handle sentinel 0x00741AD4; otherwise it only decrements and returns the 0x082067F0 status constant.

functions.name: Os_MessageQueue_Push
functions.signature: u32 Os_MessageQueue_Push(OsMessageQueue* queue, const OsMessage* msg)
functions.summary: Lock-free push of an eight-word (0x20-byte) message into a 15-slot ring buffer: copies the payload to base + 0x20 + index*0x20, issues a data-synchronisation barrier and increments the 16-bit index field (bits 8..15, modulo 15) with LDREX/STREX. When the queue goes from empty to non-empty it wakes the consumer through 0x11F730 and 0x12412C. Rejects a null queue or a kind byte >= 0xF.

functions.name: Os_VirtualToPhysical
functions.summary: Translates a virtual address to its FCRAM physical address: VRAM (0x1f000000..0x1f5fffff, plus the 0x1f600000 alias) maps to 0x08000000-based memory, the linear heap shifts by 0x0c000000 or 0x0f000000 depending on the heap base, and unmapped addresses return 0.

functions.name: Os_IpcQueryCommand18
functions.summary: Leaf IPC query on the SDK's shared session: writes command header 0x00180000 (command 0x18, no parameters) into the thread's IPC buffer and issues SVC 0x32 (SendSyncRequest); on success it copies the eight response words out and returns the reply result code. Used by the date/time query path.

functions.name: Snd_DetachChannel
functions.summary: Detaches a channel from the mixer's list: unlinks its list node at +0x110 (0x11FCBC) and clears the active word at +0x18. The mirror of the priority insert 0x11FD1C.

functions.name: std_Strncmp
functions.signature: int std_Strncmp(const u8* arg1, const u8* b, u32 len, u32 aligned)
functions.summary: Bounded string compare. While four or more bytes remain it compares whole words, using a saturating per-byte subtract against the 0x01010101 constant to detect a NUL terminator, and falls back to a byte loop for the tail; returns the difference of the first mismatching bytes (or +-1 after a byte-swapped ordering compare).

functions.name: Os_IpcSendCommand06AndClearPending
functions.summary: Forwards the selector byte to driver command 0x06 (Os_IpcSendCommand06), translates a non-success result through the 0x0011ED40 assert and then unconditionally clears the pending word at driver-session+4; called once per sampling iteration by 0x00122484.

functions.name: maybe_Os_Timer_ConvertTicks
functions.signature: void maybe_Os_Timer_ConvertTicks(s64* outMs, int stem, s64 ticksA, int stemB, u32 perSecond, int scale)
functions.summary: Converts a 64-bit tick delta to milliseconds: subtracts the two 64-bit stamps, scales by the per-second factor, converts through the double helper 0x00124ACC, rounds with 0x00125034 and stores value*1000. The 0x20C49BA5E353F7CF magic constant is the multiplicative inverse of 1000.

functions.name: Math_AlignUp
functions.signature: u32 Math_AlignUp(int stream, int offset, int extra)
functions.summary: Rounds extra+offset up to the stream's alignment (field +4) by forwarding to the shared align helper 0x0011CFAC; Ghidra dropped the real return value and shows only the extraout_r1 copy.

functions.name: Fs_ReadRecord
functions.signature: u32 Fs_ReadRecord(u32 stream, u32 offset, u32 dst, u32 maxLen, u32* read)
functions.summary: Reads a 4-byte record header (magic 0xa5 plus a 14-bit payload length) and, if the length fits in maxLen, reads the payload into dst and returns the byte count.

functions.name: maybe_Os_RefreshCachedHandle
functions.summary: Refreshes a cached kernel handle: queries the fixed IPC session (command 0x0C) for a new handle/status pair, closes the handle currently stored in *handleOut with svc 0x23, and stores the queried value there. It is a handle swap, not a counter read.

functions.name: maybe_Snd_CreateChannelBuffers
functions.signature: int maybe_Snd_CreateChannelBuffers(unsigned int width, unsigned int height, char* mode)
functions.summary: Creates the pair of buffers: when *mode is 0 it rounds both dimensions up (+4 below 0x40, +5 above, minimum 8), calls the buffer setup 0x122200 with the shared block sizes, and on failure calls 0x122484 and the session finaliser. Dead code: nothing branches to it.

functions.name: Os_IpcSendCommand0E
functions.summary: Two-parameter IPC request: command 0x0E with two normal words (value, 0xA|value<<4) and one translate buffer descriptor (buffer). Returns the reply result code.

functions.name: Svc_Ir_IpcCmd0A0000
functions.summary: Parameterless IPC request with header 0x000A0000 (command 0x0A) on the ir:USER session at 0x007B2D2C; on success it writes the second reply word (TLS+0x8C) to *out and returns the first (TLS+0x84).

functions.name: Os_IpcSendCommand19
functions.summary: Sends IPC command 0x19 (thread-local command word 0x00190040) with one parameter on the session at 0x007B2D2C and returns the reply word from TLS+0x84.

functions.name: Svc_Ir_IpcCmd180182
functions.signature: unsigned int Svc_Ir_IpcCmd180182(unsigned int handle, unsigned int firstWord, unsigned int b, unsigned int c, unsigned int d, unsigned int e, unsigned char flags)
functions.summary: Seven-word IPC submission for ir:USER command 0x18 (header 0x00180182 = one normal + six translated words): fills TLS+0x84..+0x98, puts the handle at +0xA0, issues svc 0x32 and returns the reply. Used to hand a buffer descriptor to the IR service.

functions.name: Os_IpcSendCommand0D
functions.summary: Two-parameter IPC request: command 0x0D with two normal words (value, 0x2|value<<14) and one translate buffer descriptor (buffer). Sibling of 0x00123C54; 0x001228AC picks between the two.

functions.name: Os_TranslateLinearAddress
functions.summary: Translates an address that lies inside the linear heap: validates the range against 0x124cdc/0x124cec and returns the physical address by adding the heap's base delta.

functions.name: Os_TranslateMainRamAddress
functions.summary: Returns the physical address corresponding to a range that overlaps the main-RAM window, or 0 when the range lies completely outside it.

functions.name: maybe_Os_MainRamRangeFragment
functions.summary: Not a function start: the address lies 0x196 bytes inside 0x123E18 (the main-RAM address translator) and repeats its bounds compare plus the 'base + addr' return. It only appears in the batch because a 0xB5xx halfword matched the Thumb-push scan.

functions.name: Snd_WriteChannelMatrix
functions.signature: unsigned int Snd_WriteChannelMatrix(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned int* matrix)
functions.summary: Copies twelve 32-bit words (three groups of four, from matrix-2, matrix+0xE and matrix+0x1E) into the channel block at +2, +0x12 and +0x22, then marks the block dirty with 0xE000000.

functions.name: Os_IpcSendCommand0C
functions.summary: Sends the parameterless IPC command 0x0C (TLS command word 0x000C0000) on *handleSlot and returns the reply word from TLS+0x84. Issued by Os_MessageQueue_Push as the wake-up call.

functions.name: Pack_Handle_Dtor
functions.summary: Releases the pack handle owned by a game object (a destructor helper): frees the handle's table entry, then overwrites the handle word with the 'empty' sentinel.

functions.name: Pack_ReleaseHandle
functions.summary: Releases a pack/resource handle: looks the generation-tagged handle up in the global handle table, destroys the entry when the generation matches, then overwrites the caller's word with the 'null' encoding (all low bits set) and returns the slot.

functions.name: Pack_FreeHandleEntry
functions.summary: Slow path of the handle release: decrements the entry reference count, and when it reaches zero either recycles the entry through the free list at g_0012419C or returns it to the pool allocator (0x11CFAC/0x116AE0) before unlinking it from the live list.

functions.name: Pack_HandleEntry_Init
functions.signature: void Pack_HandleEntry_Init(PackHandleEntry * entry, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
functions.summary: Constructor of a pack-handle entry: installs the vtable pair at +4/+8, clears the state words, and default-constructs the twenty 0x28-byte sub-handles at +0x18.

functions.name: Pack_LoadTableObject
functions.signature: void Pack_LoadTableObject(uint32_t* scratch, PackTableRef* out, const char* name)
functions.summary: Loads one logical table (e.g. player_param_hero.bxon) from the pack by name, validates that it is an object node (0x124E04) and stores the owned object pointer + a reference-counted handle in the 8-byte destination pair.

functions.name: Pack_LoadTableTyped
functions.signature: void Pack_LoadTableTyped(uint32_t* scratch, PackTableRef* out, const char* name)
functions.summary: Same as 0x124904 but for tables whose root node must validate against type id 0xA2 (0x124E30 + node->f_20 == 0xA2); used for the scenario_param_* family.

functions.name: Fs_ResourceFindInBucket
functions.signature: int Fs_ResourceFindInBucket(ResourceTable* self, int bucket, u32 name)
functions.summary: Scans one hash bucket of the resource table and returns the first entry that Fs_ResourceFindByName matches, or null.

functions.name: Os_IpcSendCommand06
functions.summary: Sends driver command 0x06 with one normal parameter (header 0x00060040) on the fixed session handle at 0x7B2D2C and returns the reply word.

functions.name: Os_IpcQueryCommand0C
functions.summary: Parameterless IPC query with header 0x000C0000 (command 0x0C) on the fixed session at 0x7B2D2C; on success copies the second reply word (TLS+0x8C) to *out and returns the first (TLS+0x84).

functions.name: Pack_HandlePair_MoveAssign
functions.summary: Move-assigns a pair of pack handles: releases both handles currently held by dst (validating them against the two handle tables) and then takes over src's handle, leaving src untouched.

functions.name: Fs_ResourceFindByName
functions.signature: int Fs_ResourceFindByName(ResourceTable* self, const char* name, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
functions.summary: Looks up a packed resource by name in the global resource table: hashes the bucket, then compares the 0x40-byte name key of each candidate and returns the matching record.

functions.name: Pack_GetManager
functions.summary: Returns the lazily created global pack/resource manager: an array of 0x220-byte manager slots whose first element receives the vtable at creation; every pack load goes through the returned pointer.

functions.name: maybe_std_UnwindPersonalityRoutine
functions.signature: u32 maybe_std_UnwindPersonalityRoutine(void* state, void* ucb, void* context)
functions.summary: ARM EHABI personality routine: calls the unwind bytecode interpreter 0x1250BC, whose inline opcode words follow the call site, and returns an unwind reason code. The whole 0x125098-0x125738 region is C++ exception support, not game code.

functions.name: std_MemcpyForward32
functions.signature: void* std_MemcpyForward32(void* dst, const void* src, u32 size)
functions.summary: Aligned forward memcpy: moves 32 bytes per iteration with ldm/stm plus a pld prefetch, then handles 16/8/4/2/1-byte tails. Returns the end pointers (src_end in r1, dst_end in r0).

functions.name: std_MemcpyForwardShift8
functions.signature: void* std_MemcpyForwardShift8(void* dst, const void* src, u32 size)
functions.summary: Forward memcpy for a destination one byte past word alignment: reads 8 words and re-emits them shifted by 8 bits, carrying the top byte into the next word; same 32/16/8/4/2/1 tail structure as std_MemcpyForward32.

functions.name: std_MemcpyForwardShift16
functions.signature: void* std_MemcpyForwardShift16(void* dst, const void* src, u32 size)
functions.summary: Forward memcpy for a destination two bytes off word alignment: shifts the source words by 16 bits while copying, with the usual 32/16/8/4/2/1 tails.

functions.name: std_MemcpyForwardShift24
functions.signature: void* std_MemcpyForwardShift24(void* dst, const void* src, u32 size)
functions.summary: Forward memcpy for a destination three bytes off word alignment: shifts the source words by 24 bits while copying (the last unaligned case of the family).

functions.name: std_MemmoveBackward32
functions.signature: void* std_MemmoveBackward32(void* dst_end, const void* src_end, u32 size)
functions.summary: Aligned backward (overlap-safe) memmove: walks down in 32-byte steps with ldmdb/stmdb and a pld prefetch, then the 16/8/4/2/1 tails.

functions.name: std_MemmoveBackwardShift8
functions.signature: void* std_MemmoveBackwardShift8(void* dst_end, const void* src_end, u32 size)
functions.summary: Backward memmove for a destination one byte off word alignment: shifts the descending word stream by 8 bits, then finishes with the 4/2/1 tails.

functions.name: std_MemmoveBackwardShift16
functions.signature: void* std_MemmoveBackwardShift16(void* dst_end, const void* src_end, u32 size)
functions.summary: Backward memmove with a 16-bit shift between source and destination words, used when the destination is two bytes off alignment.

functions.name: std_MemmoveBackwardShift24
functions.signature: void* std_MemmoveBackwardShift24(void* dst_end, const void* src_end, u32 size)
functions.summary: Backward memmove with a 24-bit shift between source and destination words (destination three bytes off alignment); last member of the overlap-safe copy family.

functions.name: maybe_std_CopyPointerListAndSync
functions.summary: Copies a count-driven array of double-dereferenced pointers (desc[1] holds the array, desc[2] the count) into the caller's buffer; for a count of exactly one it instead clears the first word and issues svc 0x24 (wait for one handle).

functions.name: std_UInt64Divide
functions.signature: unsigned long long std_UInt64Divide(unsigned int numLo, unsigned int numHi, unsigned int denLo, unsigned int denHi)
functions.summary: Unsigned 64/64-bit division helper: normalises both operands, uses the reciprocal table at 0x126108 for the quotient estimate and corrects the remainder, returning the 64-bit quotient; returns 0 (or traps) when the denominator is zero or the quotient overflows.

functions.name: std_Int64Divide
functions.signature: long long std_Int64Divide(int numLo, int numHi, int denLo, int denHi)
functions.summary: Signed 64/64-bit division wrapper: takes the absolute values of both operands (using the sign bits), calls the unsigned core 0x125E58 and negates the quotient when the operand signs differ.

functions.name: std_MemCopyAlias
functions.signature: u32 std_MemCopyAlias(const void * src, void * dst, u32 bytes)
functions.summary: Alternate entry to the forward memcpy (0x116a14) that forwards its three arguments and returns the destination; i.e. a second memcpy symbol from another translation unit.

functions.name: std_VfpSaveRestoreState
functions.summary: Compiler VFP context helper (two entry labels): saves d8-d15 into a caller buffer / restores them, used by the soft-float and exception-support code. Ghidra merged the save and restore halves into one 'function' because the save half ends in bx lr but the restore half follows immediately.

functions.name: std_DoubleDivideCore
functions.signature: u64 std_DoubleDivideCore(u32 q_lo, u32 n_hi, u32 n_lo, u32 d_hi, u32 d_lo)
functions.summary: Software double-precision division core: normalises the operands with a reciprocal byte table, runs the Newton-Raphson quotient refinement and the four 16-bit long-division steps, then assembles the result exponent/mantissa. Only reachable from the soft-float helpers around it.

functions.name: std_ScalbnDouble
functions.signature: double std_ScalbnDouble(u32 lo, u32 hi, u32 mant, int exponent)
functions.summary: Double-precision scalbn/ldexp: shifts the mantissa by the requested exponent and rebuilds the IEEE-754 word, returning the input unchanged when the resulting exponent field stays inside the normal range (0x000-0x7FF).

functions.name: maybe_std_ScalbnRoundTail
functions.signature: double maybe_std_ScalbnRoundTail(u32 sign, u32 mantissaHigh, u32 mantissaLow, int exponent)
functions.summary: Rounding/overflow tail of the double-precision scalbn helper: increments the mantissa high word, propagates a carry into the exponent and saturates to infinity, returning the packed double sign|exponent. It is a branch target inside 0x126728, not a stand-alone API.

functions.name: std_DoubleDivide
functions.signature: void std_DoubleDivide(const double* lhs, const double* rhs, int mode, double* out)
functions.summary: Soft-float double divide wrapper: if both operands are finite normal numbers it runs the mantissa divide core (exponent subtraction) and returns the packed double; special values are left to the caller.

functions.name: std_DoubleMultiply
functions.signature: void std_DoubleMultiply(const double* lhs, const double* rhs, int mode, double* out)
functions.summary: Soft-float double multiply wrapper: for two finite normal operands it runs the mantissa multiply core (exponent addition) and returns the packed double.

functions.name: std_DoubleMultiplyCore
functions.signature: u64 std_DoubleMultiplyCore(u32 p_lo, u32 a_hi, u32 a_lo, u32 b_hi, u32 b_lo)
functions.summary: Software double-precision multiply core: splits both operands into 16-bit limbs, accumulates the cross products with carry propagation, applies the sign correction and returns the normalised 64-bit product. Companion of std_DoubleDivideCore.

functions.name: maybe_Video_ConvertBlocks32_SamePlane
functions.summary: In-place colour/format conversion over four lanes 0x400 bytes apart: reads 8 packed bytes per step from src+0x2000, combines them with saturating 8-bit difference/average arithmetic and the two per-channel constants at +0x10/+0x14, and writes the result back to the same buffer. Outer count f_c-8, inner count (context+8)-8.

functions.name: maybe_Video_ConvertBlocks32_A
functions.summary: Common second stage of the second conversion family, always run after the selected variant: reads 8 packed bytes per step from src+0x20 and the three lanes at +0x404/+0x804/+0xC04, converts them with saturating difference/average arithmetic and the per-channel constants, and writes backwards into the lanes at +0x408/+0x808/+0xC08. Outer count (context+8)-0x20, inner count f_c.

functions.name: maybe_Video_ConvertBlocks16_A
functions.summary: Same conversion on 16-byte blocks: reads six lanes 0x400 bytes apart (src+0x2000 with offsets -0xC00..+0x800), averages neighbouring bytes and saturates the differences, with an outer count of f_c-8 and an inner count of (context+8)-0x10. Selected by the dispatcher 0x0012A81C when the context's two pointers are equal.

functions.name: maybe_Video_ConvertBlocks32B_A
functions.summary: Common second stage of the first conversion family, always run after the selected variant: same four-lane read/write pattern with an outer count of f_c (not f_c-8) and a different byte unpack. Twin at 0x12BF58.

functions.name: maybe_Video_ConvertPlanes4_A
functions.summary: Plane-oriented member of the conversion family: takes an explicit four-field descriptor (source, destination, length, plane count), loops four times over the plane pointers with a 0x400-byte plane stride and a 0x3e0 row offset, and converts each plane with the same saturating colour arithmetic. Selected by 0x0012A81C when the two pointers differ.

functions.name: maybe_Video_ConvertPlanes3_A
functions.summary: Sibling of 0x001290A0 with the same four-field descriptor and 4x-unrolled plane loop but a shorter body; selected by the second dispatcher 0x0012A84C (the 'pointers are equal' branch). Twin at 0x12DC6C.

functions.name: Video_ConvertSelect_A
functions.summary: Dispatcher of the first conversion family: when the context's two leading pointers differ it runs the plane variant 0x1290A0, otherwise the 16-byte block variant 0x12762C, and then always runs the common 32-byte stage 0x1281E0.

functions.name: Video_ConvertSelectB_A
functions.summary: Dispatcher of the second conversion family: picks the 8-byte in-place variant 0x126B0C or the three-plane variant 0x129EF4 on the same 'pointers differ' test, then always runs the 32-byte stage 0x126EF4.

functions.name: maybe_Video_ConvertBlocks8_B
functions.summary: 8-byte-block member of the family (copy B): reads four lanes 0x100 bytes apart (src+0x800 with u32 offsets -0x80/-0x40/0/+0x40), 8 bytes per step, outer count f_c-8 and inner count (context+8)-8; the smallest member of the family.

functions.name: Video_ConvertBlocks32_B
functions.summary: In-place pixel-format conversion in 32-byte (0x20) steps: reads four lanes 0x400 bytes apart, rewrites each byte with saturating average/difference arithmetic using two caller-supplied per-channel constants, and stores back into the same buffer. One of the five converter variants the class dispatcher picks between. Byte-compared with the twin at 0x00126EF4 (Video_ConvertBlocks32_A): 77 of 1848 bytes differ, but the decompiled body is identical, so the copy is the same routine with relocated constants/addresses.

functions.name: Video_ConvertBlocks16_B
functions.summary: Same in-place conversion as Video_ConvertBlocks32 but on 16-byte (0x10) steps with an outer count of f_c-8, i.e. the variant used when the class header says the two plane pointers differ. Byte-compared with the twin at 0x0012762C (Video_ConvertBlocks16_A): 103 of 2996 bytes differ, but the decompiled body is identical, so the copy is the same routine with relocated constants/addresses.

functions.name: Video_ConvertBlocks32B_B
functions.summary: Second 32-byte-step converter of the family: different byte-parameter unpack and an outer count of f_c instead of f_c-8. Note the "B" in Blocks32B means "second variant"; the trailing _B/_C on the name is the code copy, not the variant. Byte-compared with the twin at 0x001281E0 (Video_ConvertBlocks32B_A): 151 of 3776 bytes differ, but the decompiled body is identical, so the copy is the same routine with relocated constants/addresses.

functions.name: maybe_Video_ConvertPlanes4_B
functions.summary: Plane-descriptor member of the converter class: takes a four-field descriptor (source plane, destination plane, count, plane count) and runs the same saturating per-byte conversion over its planes, with a 0x100-byte plane stride and a 0xe0 row offset (the A copy uses 0x400/0x3e0).

functions.name: maybe_Video_ConvertPlanes3_B
functions.summary: Second plane-descriptor converter, selected by the other dispatcher branch; same four-field descriptor and 4x-unrolled loop as the Planes4 member but a shorter body, with a 0x100-byte plane stride and a 0xe0 row offset. What actually distinguishes the '3' from the '4' is still unknown.

functions.name: Video_ConvertSelect_B
functions.summary: First class dispatcher: chooses between the 16-byte converter and the plane-descriptor converter on a pointer-equality test in the class header, then always runs the second 32-byte converter. 48 bytes, no arithmetic of its own. Byte-compared with the twin at 0x0012A81C (Video_ConvertSelect_A): byte-identical (48 bytes).

functions.name: Video_ConvertSelectB_B
functions.summary: Second class dispatcher: chooses between the 8-byte converter and the three-plane converter on the same pointer test, then always runs Video_ConvertBlocks32. Byte-compared with the twin at 0x0012A84C (Video_ConvertSelectB_A): 4 of 56 bytes differ, but the decompiled body is identical, so the copy is the same routine with relocated constants/addresses.

functions.name: Video_ConvertBlocks8_C
functions.summary: Smallest member of the converter family: 8-byte steps over the same four lanes, with one lane inverted (~uVar64) and an outer count of f_c-8. This is the copy the live game path reaches, through the merged dispatcher blob at 0x0013233C. Byte-compared with the twin at 0x00126B0C (Video_ConvertBlocks32_SamePlane): 29 of 1000 bytes differ, but the decompiled body is identical, so the copy is the same routine with relocated constants/addresses.

functions.name: Video_ConvertBlocks32_C
functions.summary: In-place pixel-format conversion in 32-byte (0x20) steps: reads four lanes 0x400 bytes apart, rewrites each byte with saturating average/difference arithmetic using two caller-supplied per-channel constants, and stores back into the same buffer. One of the five converter variants the class dispatcher picks between. Byte-compared with the twin at 0x0012AC6C (Video_ConvertBlocks32_B): 77 of 1848 bytes differ, but the decompiled body is identical, so the copy is the same routine with relocated constants/addresses.

functions.name: Video_ConvertBlocks16_C
functions.summary: Same in-place conversion as Video_ConvertBlocks32 but on 16-byte (0x10) steps with an outer count of f_c-8, i.e. the variant used when the class header says the two plane pointers differ. Byte-compared with the twin at 0x0012762C (Video_ConvertBlocks16_A): 103 of 2996 bytes differ, but the decompiled body is identical, so the copy is the same routine with relocated constants/addresses.

functions.name: Video_ConvertBlocks32B_C
functions.summary: Second 32-byte-step converter of the family: different byte-parameter unpack and an outer count of f_c instead of f_c-8. Note the "B" in Blocks32B means "second variant"; the trailing _B/_C on the name is the code copy, not the variant. Byte-compared with the twin at 0x0012BF58 (Video_ConvertBlocks32B_B): 151 of 3776 bytes differ, but the decompiled body is identical, so the copy is the same routine with relocated constants/addresses.

functions.name: maybe_Video_ConvertPlanes4_C
functions.summary: Plane-descriptor member of the converter class: takes a four-field descriptor (source plane, destination plane, count, plane count) and runs the same saturating per-byte conversion over its planes, with a 0x200-byte plane stride and a 0x1e0 row offset (A uses 0x400/0x3e0, B uses 0x100/0xe0).

functions.name: maybe_Video_ConvertPlanes3_C
functions.summary: Second plane-descriptor converter, selected by the other dispatcher branch; same four-field descriptor and 4x-unrolled loop as the Planes4 member but a shorter body, with a 0x200-byte plane stride and a 0x1e0 row offset. What actually distinguishes the '3' from the '4' is still unknown.

functions.name: Video_ConvertSelect_C

functions.name: Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock
functions.summary: Decodes one block of transform coefficients: picks the DC predictor from the block-type bits, then walks the block row by row feeding every bit through the two interleaved VLC case bodies (0x001351C8 when the bit is set, 0x00135104 when clear) and refilling the bit reservoir as needed. Returns the number of bits consumed, which the caller uses to advance the stream. functions.name: maybe_Video_DecodeCoefficientGroupOdd

functions.name: maybe_Video_CoefficientSwitchTail1

functions.name: Video_IdctBlock8x8

The mask byte is read through the fixed table address 0x08010400 and the register r6 is an incoming value, so this is a mid-function entry, not a stand-alone API.

functions.name: Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock_B
functions.summary: Decodes one block of transform coefficients: picks the DC predictor from the block-type bits, then walks the block row by row feeding every bit through the two interleaved VLC case bodies (0x001351C8 when the bit is set, 0x00135104 when clear) and refilling the bit reservoir as needed. Returns the number of bits consumed, which the caller uses to advance the stream. Byte-compared with the twin at 0x00134EE4 (Video_DecodeCoefficientBlock): 2 of 544 bytes differ, but the decompiled body is identical, so the copy is the same routine with relocated constants/addresses.

functions.name: maybe_Video_DecodeCoefficientGroupEven_B
functions.signature: void maybe_Video_DecodeCoefficientGroupEven_B(u32 block, u32 subblock, int bitCount, u32 bitReservoir)
functions.summary: Second copy of the block decoder's 'even' VLC case body (copy 1 is 0x135104): takes three bits from the bit reservoir, remaps the escape code and jumps through the relocated 16-entry table at 0x13B6C4 to decode one interleaved coefficient group. Only 2 of 0xC4 bytes differ from copy 1 (the literal pool moved), and its bit-reservoir helpers are the second copies at 0x13BE38/0x13BE68.

functions.name: maybe_Video_DecodeCoefficientGroupOdd_B
functions.signature: void maybe_Video_DecodeCoefficientGroupOdd_B(u32 block, u32 subblock, int bitCount, u32 bitReservoir)
functions.summary: Second copy of the block decoder's 'odd' case body (copy 1 is 0x1351C8): takes a 4-bit prefix, clamps the code index against the subblock's remaining counts (f_51/f_58), rewrites the four current-code bytes at +0x59/+0x5A/+0x61/+0x62 and jumps through the relocated table at 0x13BA18. Same size as copy 1 with 2 differing bytes.

functions.name: Video_DecodeSubblockMask_B
functions.summary: Walks the current sub-block's coefficient-presence mask: reads the mask byte for the sub-block index left in r6 and calls the per-slot decoder 0x0013562C once for every set bit (bits 1..0x20). Runs before the VLC decoding of that sub-block. Byte-compared with the twin at 0x001352A0 (Video_DecodeSubblockMask): 18 of 660 bytes differ, but the decompiled body is identical, so the copy is the same routine with relocated constants/addresses.

functions.name: maybe_Video_VlcDispatchEntry_B
functions.summary: Track B duplicate of maybe_Video_VlcDispatchEntry: VLC coefficient-switch case entry in the secondary video decoder pipeline.

functions.name: maybe_Video_CoefficientSwitchTail1_B
functions.summary: Track B duplicate of maybe_Video_CoefficientSwitchTail1: shared 36-byte tail of the VLC coefficient-decode switch in the secondary pipeline.

functions.name: Video_IdctBlock8x8_B
functions.summary: Reconstructs one 8x8 luma block: zeroes the 64-word coefficient array, lets 0x001377A0 fill it, then runs the integer inverse transform (8-point butterfly with the >>1/>>2 twiddle approximations and a >>6 output scale) and writes the 8 samples of each of the eight 0x400-spaced lanes. Three block-type thresholds select a DC-only, a reduced-coefficient and the full transform path. Byte-compared with the twin at 0x0013563C (Video_ResidualBlockAdd): byte-identical (152 bytes).

functions.name: maybe_Video_IdctSubblocks_B
functions.summary: Second copy of the per-mask 4x4 inverse-transform loop: runs Video_IdctBlock4x4_B once for each set bit (1, 2, 4, 8) of the current sub-block mask byte. Template copy of 0x001356D4 with relocated constants (the two bodies differ in 2 of 84 bytes), entered mid-function.

functions.name: maybe_Video_CoefficientSwitchTail2_B
functions.summary: Track B duplicate of maybe_Video_CoefficientSwitchTail2: second shared 24-byte tail of the VLC coefficient-decode switch in the secondary pipeline.

functions.name: maybe_Video_VlcDispatchEntry2_B
functions.summary: Jump-table dispatch block of the coefficient VLC loop: takes the code index in r12, adds 10 and jumps through the relocated 0x00135418 table after testing the flag byte at 0x02000F00[r6]. Same body as the twin at 0x00135740 (maybe_Video_VlcDispatchEntry2); the block is entered from the coefficient switch tail, so 'Entry2' is a positional label, not a proven role.

functions.name: Video_IdctBlock4x4_B
functions.summary: Chroma counterpart of Video_IdctBlock8x8: zeroes a 16-word coefficient array, then runs a 4-point inverse transform and writes four samples into each of four 0x400-spaced lanes (the 4x4 chroma block of a YUV 4:2:0 macroblock). DC-only and reduced-coefficient paths are selected the same way. Byte-compared with the twin at 0x001357E8 (Video_ResidualBlockAdd2): byte-identical (212 bytes).

functions.name: Video_InterpolateBlock4x4_B
functions.summary: Sub-pixel interpolator of the video decoder: reads four neighbouring packed source words plus the byte one row up, runs a 6-bit fixed-point DDA per byte lane with +0x40>>7 rounding over 16 output samples and writes four packed words. The 0x400 pitch and the taps are the motion-compensation filter kernel.

functions.name: Video_InterpolateBlock2x2_B
functions.summary: Half-resolution sibling of Video_InterpolateBlock4x4: the same 6-bit fixed-point DDA, but over the 0x200 lanes with two output samples per step, which is what the '2x2' refers to.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesDiag_B
functions.summary: Diagonal neighbour blend of the prediction block: reads the samples at -1, +0xFF, +0x1FF, +0x2FF (and further 0x100 steps in the unrolled tail) and writes 1:2:1 and (a+2b+c+2)>>2 averages as packed words into the lanes 0x100 above.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesRow_B
functions.summary: Horizontal blend with a one-row-up source kernel: takes the two packed words one lane up (r11-0x100, r11-0xFC) plus the byte at -1 and writes the 1:2:1 averaged packed word at *r11, then repeats down the row.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesRow2_B
functions.summary: Row-wide unrolled blend kernel: the same 1:2:1 averaging over the 0x100-spaced lanes, unrolled over a whole row of packed words so every intermediate stays in registers.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesRow3_B
functions.summary: Second row-wide unrolled blend kernel: averages the 0x100-spaced lanes together with the horizontally adjacent packed words over a whole row.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesBlock_B
functions.summary: Block-wide unrolled blend kernel: the same 1:2:1 lane averaging expanded over a whole block so every intermediate stays in registers.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesFromStream_B
functions.summary: Blend variant used inside the coefficient loop: first advances the decoder state through 0x0013587C and then averages the four lanes into the packed words above.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesCorner1_B
functions.summary: Corner (up-left) predictor kernel: averages the up-left byte (-0x101), the left byte (-1) and the two packed words one lane up.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesCorner2_B
functions.summary: Mirrored corner predictor kernel: the same -0x101/-1/lane-up taps with a different tap order.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesCorner3_B
functions.summary: Third corner predictor kernel: the same inputs as Video_BlendPlanesCorner1 with the smallest tap set of the three.

functions.name: Video_FilterPackedBytesRow_B
functions.summary: Per-byte-lane 1:2:1 filter over packed 32-bit words: walks a whole scanline, averaging each byte with its horizontal neighbour and with the byte one row up (r11-0x100) and repacking four samples per word. The four bytes of a word are four consecutive samples, so this is a sample filter, not a per-channel pixel operation.

functions.name: Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4_B
functions.summary: Per-byte-lane 1:2:1 filter over packed 32-bit words: masks four packed words with 0x7F7F7F7F, halves them and recombines with the carry of the next word, a SIMD horizontal 1:2:1 over 16 consecutive samples.

functions.name: Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4b_B
functions.summary: Per-byte-lane 1:2:1 filter over packed 32-bit words: the same mask-and-average over four words taken in the opposite order.

functions.name: Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4c_B
functions.summary: Per-byte-lane 1:2:1 filter over packed 32-bit words: the same per-byte average on unaligned byte offsets (-1, +3, +7, +0xB), i.e. over a diagonally shifted sample run.

functions.name: Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4d_B
functions.summary: Per-byte-lane 1:2:1 filter over packed 32-bit words: fourth member of the unaligned family, same per-byte average.

functions.name: Video_FilterPackedBytesBlock_B
functions.summary: Per-byte-lane 1:2:1 filter over packed 32-bit words: keeps 15 pointers/accumulators live and applies the mask-and-average to a whole block instead of four words.

functions.name: Video_FilterPackedBytesBlock2_B
functions.summary: Per-byte-lane 1:2:1 filter over packed 32-bit words: smaller sibling of Video_FilterPackedBytesBlock with fewer live accumulators.

functions.name: Video_FilterPackedBytesFrame_B
functions.summary: Per-byte-lane 1:2:1 filter over packed 32-bit words: applies the mask-and-average over a whole frame, walking the four 0x400-spaced lanes (self+1, +0x401, +0x801, +0xC01) with 0x7F7F7F7F as the per-byte lane mask so no lane carries into the next.

functions.name: Video_DecodeSubblockMask_C
functions.summary: Decodes the sub-block coefficient-presence mask in track C: reads mask byte for sub-block in r6 from table 0x01040F00 and calls per-slot decoder once for each set bit.

functions.name: maybe_Video_VlcDispatchEntry_C
functions.summary: VLC coefficient-switch case entry in track C: reads bit reservoir and branches through jump table based on sub-block flag byte.

functions.name: maybe_Video_CoefficientSwitchTail1_C
functions.summary: Shared 36-byte tail of the VLC coefficient-decode switch in track C: indirect jump through the relative jump table using code index in in_r12.

functions.name: Video_IdctBlock8x8_C
functions.summary: Inverse discrete cosine transform for 8x8 luma blocks in track C: zeroes 64-word coefficient array, runs 8-point butterfly integer inverse transform, and writes 8 samples to eight 0x200-spaced lanes.

functions.name: maybe_Video_IdctSubblocks_C
functions.summary: Sub-block 4x4 inverse transform loop in track C: reads sub-block mask byte at 0x08010400[unaff_r6] and calls Video_IdctBlock4x4_C once for each set bit (1, 2, 4, 8).

functions.name: maybe_Video_CoefficientSwitchTail2_C
functions.summary: Second shared 24-byte tail of the VLC coefficient-decode switch in track C: relative jump through jump table using code index in in_r12.

functions.name: maybe_Video_VlcDispatchEntry2_C
functions.summary: Second jump-table dispatch entry of coefficient VLC loop in track C: adds 10 to code index in in_r12 and jumps through table after testing flag byte.

functions.name: Video_IdctBlock4x4_C
functions.summary: Chroma counterpart 4x4 inverse discrete cosine transform in track C: zeroes 16-word coefficient array, runs 4-point inverse transform butterflies, and stores to four 0x200-spaced lanes.

functions.name: Video_InterpolateBlock4x4_C
functions.summary: Sub-pixel interpolator for 4x4 blocks in track C: reads neighbouring packed source words, runs 6-bit fixed-point DDA per byte lane with +0x40>>7 rounding, writing packed words over 0x200-stride lanes.

functions.name: Video_InterpolateBlock2x2_C
functions.summary: Half-resolution 2x2 sub-pixel interpolator in track C: 6-bit fixed-point DDA over 0x100-stride lanes with two output samples per step for chroma block interpolation.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesDiag_C
functions.summary: Diagonal neighbour blend of prediction block in track C: reads samples at -1, +0x1FF, +0x3FF, +0x5FF and writes 1:2:1 and (a+2b+c+2)>>2 averages as packed words into 0x200 lanes.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesRow_C
functions.summary: Horizontal blend with one-row-up source kernel in track C: takes two packed words one lane up (r11-0x200, r11-0x1FC) plus byte at -1 and writes 1:2:1 averaged packed words across row.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesRow2_C
functions.summary: Second unrolled row blend variant in track C: 1:2:1 averaging over 0x200-spaced lanes, unrolled across full scanline of packed samples.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesRow3_C
functions.summary: Third row blend variant in track C: averages 0x200-spaced lanes and horizontally adjacent packed words.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesBlock_C
functions.summary: Block-wide unrolled blend kernel in track C: expands 1:2:1 lane averaging over entire block with all intermediates held in CPU registers.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesFromStream_C
functions.summary: Stream-driven plane blend kernel in track C: advances bitstream via func_0014247C before averaging four 0x200-spaced sample lanes.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesCorner1_C
functions.summary: Corner-prediction kernel variant 1 in track C: averages up-left byte (-0x201), left byte (-1), and packed words one lane up into destination at *r11.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesCorner2_C
functions.summary: Mirrored corner-prediction kernel variant 2 in track C: averages -0x201, -1, and lane-up terms with reversed tap order.

functions.name: Video_BlendPlanesCorner3_C
functions.summary: Corner-prediction kernel variant 3 in track C: minimal tap set averaging -0x201, -1, and lane-up terms.

functions.name: Video_FilterPackedBytesRow_C
functions.summary: Per-byte-lane 1:2:1 filter over packed 32-bit sample words in track C: walks scanline averaging each byte with horizontal neighbour and row up (r11-0x200).

functions.name: Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4_C
functions.summary: Four-word packed-sample filter in track C: masks four input words with 0x7F7F7F7F, shifts down by 1, and recombines without cross-lane carries.

functions.name: Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4b_C
functions.summary: Second four-word packed-sample filter in track C: same 0x7F7F7F7F mask-and-average scheme with words processed in reverse order.

functions.name: Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4c_C
functions.summary: Third packed-sample filter in track C: operates on unaligned byte offsets (-1, +3, +7, +0xB) to filter diagonally neighbouring samples with 0x7F7F7F7F lane mask.

functions.name: Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4d_C
functions.summary: Fourth packed-sample filter of unaligned family in track C: 0x7F7F7F7F mask and average across offset sample words.

functions.name: Video_FilterPackedBytesBlock_C
functions.summary: Multi-row packed-sample block filter in track C: maintains multiple accumulator pointers applying 0x7F7F7F7F mask-and-average scheme across block.

functions.name: Video_FilterPackedBytesBlock2_C
functions.summary: Smaller multi-row packed-sample block filter in track C: 0x7F7F7F7F mask-and-average filtering with reduced accumulator set.

functions.name: Video_FilterPackedBytesFrame_C
functions.summary: Full-frame packed-sample filter entry point in track C: applies 0x7F7F7F7F mask-and-average sample filter across 0x200-spaced lanes over entire frame.

functions.name: Actor_Component_CheckNotify

functions.summary: Per-frame update for the gold window: ticks the window's sub-objects, advances the 0x18-byte entry array (up to 0x0C entries) with its vtable callbacks, and clears the pending-close flag when finished.

functions.name: Ui_GoldWindow_SetOwner
functions.signature: void Ui_GoldWindow_SetOwner(UiGoldWindow* self, uint32_t owner, uint8_t visible)

functions.name: Actor_Node_SetVisibleAll
functions.signature: void Actor_Node_SetVisibleAll(ActorComponent* self, u32 flag, u32 p1, u32 p2)

functions.name: maybe_Actor_Node_InitState

functions.summary: Actor component vtable method (vtable 0x007290C0): checks actor state byte f_48C and configures node state at self+0x488.

functions.name: Ui_DialogUpdateQueue
functions.signature: u32 Ui_DialogUpdateQueue(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

functions.name: maybe_Actor_Node_CheckBounds
functions.summary: Actor component vtable method (vtable 0x00729028): coordinate/bounds comparison on actor component.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_DialogAdvance
functions.signature: u32 maybe_Ui_DialogAdvance(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

functions.name: Actor_Node_ShowVariantA
functions.summary: Virtual method in actor vtable 0x00729088 that turns on visibility for the actor render node at +0x32C.

functions.name: Actor_Node_UpdateVariantA
functions.summary: Per-frame update virtual method in actor vtable 0x00729090 that updates motion state at +0x488 when in state 2, 3, 4, or 5 and notifies listeners.

functions.name: Actor_Node_ShowVariantB

functions.name: Actor_Node_ShowVariantC
functions.summary: Virtual method in actor vtable 0x00729078 that sets visibility to 1 on the actor node at +0x32C.

functions.name: Text_SetSpeakerNameArg

functions.summary: Installs the current speaker's name as message argument 5 and copies the speaker/party strings into the dialog's text buffers.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_DialogAdvance2
functions.signature: u32 maybe_Ui_DialogAdvance2(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
functions.summary: Second dialog page-transition variant: uses the alternate page object at +0x3C4, resets it through maybe_Ui_FourRowList_ResetFromStateB, and sends page command 7 after 0x006122F0(bag,id) when the pending id at +0x468 is set.

functions.name: Actor_Node_ShowVariantD
functions.summary: Virtual method in actor vtable 0x00729038 that sets visibility to 1 on the actor node at +0x32C.

functions.name: Actor_Node_ShowVariantE
functions.summary: Virtual method in actor vtable 0x00729098 that sets visibility to 1 on the actor node at +0x32C.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_DialogAdvance3
functions.signature: u32 maybe_Ui_DialogAdvance3(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
functions.summary: Third dialog page-transition variant: reads the mask at +0x120, resets the four-row page through maybe_Ui_FourRowList_ResetFromStateA and dispatches page commands 1/3 through the vtable at self+0x47.

functions.name: Actor_Node_UpdateVariantB
functions.summary: Update virtual method in actor vtable 0x007290A0 that refreshes motion state at +0x488 for states 2..5 and notifies listeners at +0x11C.

functions.name: Actor_Node_ShowVariantF
functions.summary: Virtual method in actor vtable 0x007290A8 that sets visibility to 1 on the actor node at +0x32C.

functions.name: Actor_Node_UpdateVariantD
functions.summary: Actor-node vtable slot 0x007290B0: reads the state byte at self+0x48C and, when it is 2/3/4/5, refreshes the motion node at self+0x488 through 0x0062B24C, stores the result byte at self+0x49C, asks the owner (virtual +0x11C -> +0x14) whether to continue and then fires virtual +0x10; always returns 1.

functions.name: Actor_Node_ShowVariantG
functions.summary: Virtual method in actor vtable 0x00729058 that sets visibility to 1 on the actor node at +0x32C.

functions.name: Actor_Node_UpdateVariantE
functions.summary: Actor-node vtable slot 0x00729060: same state-check-and-notify step as Actor_Node_UpdateVariantB/D - state byte self+0x48C in {2,3,4,5} refreshes the motion node at self+0x488 via 0x0062B24C, writes self+0x49C, then calls the owner virtual +0x11C -> +0x14 and, if it agrees, virtual +0x10; returns 1.

functions.name: Actor_Node_ShowVariantH
functions.summary: Virtual method in actor vtable 0x00729068 that sets visibility to 1 on the actor node at +0x32C.

functions.name: Actor_Node_UpdateVariantC
functions.summary: Update virtual method in actor vtable 0x00729070 that updates motion state at +0x488 and notifies listeners at +0x11C.

functions.name: Actor_Node_ShowVariantI
functions.summary: Virtual method in actor vtable 0x007290B8 that sets visibility to 1 on the actor node at +0x32C.

functions.name: Party_Member_SetNameArg
functions.signature: void Party_Member_SetNameArg(void* dialog, int memberIndex, int arg3)
functions.summary: Selects party member by index and sets their name string as message argument 5 for dialog display.

functions.name: Ui_Window_InitBase
functions.summary: Base constructor of a UI window: creates the window object through 0x1d8b6c, installs its vtable, then creates the 12-entry child list object at +0x11c and back-links it to the window.

functions.name: Ui_CreateRootSingleton
functions.summary: Constructs the engine-wide UI root object in place: installs the root vtable, builds five layout-animation children, a screen controller, several pane groups and the resource handle, then links them into the root's intrusive lists. Called once, from the shutdown/atexit counterpart 0x10F6BC.

functions.name: Battle_CalcTurnOrderPriority
functions.summary: Computes a battle unit's turn-order agility roll: fetches effective Agility via 0x0048F08C(battleUnit), multiplies by a uniform random factor in [0.51f, 1.0f] from BattleScene RNG (+0x4218 via 0x001CA3E4), and returns the truncated integer priority.

functions.name: maybe_Field_InitSharedParams
functions.summary: One-time initialiser guarded by self->f_E4 == 0: allocates a 500-byte object, installs vtable 0x0075A7D4 and constructs a 19 x 24-byte array from 0x006C3354. The rest of the body is Ghidra absolute-address garbage (_DAT_00000020, 0x00726AA8->f_7C), so the 'shared params' reading is unproven.

functions.name: Field_Gimmick_TriggerEvent3
functions.summary: Dispatches event type 3 to the gimmick controller state machine at +0xE4 with parameter value stored in field 0xFC.

functions.name: Field_Gimmick_TriggerEvent15
functions.summary: Dispatches event type 0x0F (15) to the gimmick controller state machine at +0xE4 with parameter value stored in field 0xFC.

functions.name: Ui_CmdQueue_ClearSlot
functions.summary: Resets one slot of the UI command queue: zeroes the 0x8C-byte entry, sets the event id and three state words to -1 and cancels the running command.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_Widget_Reset
functions.summary: Resets a UI window: clears +0xF2, clears slot 0x53 unless the battle mode byte (+0x4248) is 1, calls vtable +0x20 and clears f_3F.

functions.name: Field_Gimmick_CheckActiveNodes
functions.summary: Iterates over linked nodes in list self->f_110 and verifies active status flags via table lookup func_00630DC8.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_CommandSlots_UpdateContinuationA
functions.summary: First split fragment of the battle command-slot update (routine at 0x00168C64): walks the five 0x8C-byte command slots of the current actor, dispatches each slot's vtable method, resolves the target through the party list and resets the slot records.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_CommandSlots_UpdateContinuationB
functions.summary: Second split fragment of the same battle command-slot update: the loop body that dispatches each queued slot's vtable method, creates the per-slot command object from the 0x7A4338/0x7A4268 tables and queues the action entry.

functions.name: Ui_CmdQueue_PushWidgetCommand
functions.signature: void Ui_CmdQueue_PushWidgetCommand(UiQueue* self, UiWidget* widget, u32 command, code* callback)
functions.summary: Queues a command against one widget: checks the widget is active, computes the scaled parameter, appends the command record and either invokes the callback immediately or stores the result in the widget's per-state byte.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_CommandSlots_TryDecrement
functions.summary: Tries to step the battle manager's stored command slots back: for each of the four 3-byte slots (id/arg/arg2 at +0xFD/+0x100/+0x103/+0x106) whose id is 5 it decrements the third byte, then validates the result with Battle_CheckUnitCommandCondition(self, 5) and restores all four values when the condition fails.

functions.name: Field_Gimmick_TriggerEvent14
functions.summary: Dispatches event type 0x0E (14) to the gimmick controller state machine at +0xE4 with parameter value stored in field 0xFC.

functions.name: Ui_CmdQueue_ProcessSlots
functions.summary: Processes the queued UI commands of the current frame: first checks the pending-command hook, then walks every 0x8C-byte slot, calls the widget vtable slots and matches the event id against the global window list before dispatching.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_Ui_ApplyUnitMessageText
functions.summary: For every unit in the battle party list (+0x4260), resolves the unit's character byte at +0x768 to a party record and, for each of the record's four byte pairs at +0x370, rolls an id in that range with the battle RNG and pushes it to the unit's widget through vtable +0x40; a final value from the record's +0x398 float is pushed the same way.

functions.name: Battle_QueueCommand0x15
functions.signature: void Battle_QueueCommand0x15(void* queue, u32* action, u32* out)
functions.summary: Pushes battle command 0x15: computes the turn-order priority with Battle_CalcTurnOrderPriority, derives two flag words from the action (byte table at 0x00169DBC, mode byte f_10, byte +0xB108) and appends the entry through Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry with mode 7.

functions.name: Battle_AreAllUnitsIdle
functions.summary: Returns 1 when none of the up to 4x26 battle units (lists at work+8->+0x5C +0x428C, resolved with 0x002AB62C) without flags 0x46 is still busy (vtable +0x18 or +0x10); otherwise 0.

functions.name: Field_Gimmick_OnZoneChange
functions.summary: Notifies the gimmick state machine of zone or position transition by sending event 10 with flag 1 or 8 based on zone matching.

functions.name: Battle_DispatchEventToUnits
functions.signature: void Battle_DispatchEventToUnits(void* self, u32 event, u32 argument, void* callback)
functions.summary: Walks every active unit in battle work +0x4270 unit list, builds 0xB0-byte event structure, and dispatches to unit callback.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_IsUnitSoundFinished
functions.summary: Returns 1 only when every unit in the four battle unit lists has finished its sound: per unit it checks the widget state (8), the 0x20000000 flag and the remaining playback time, returning 0 as soon as one is still running.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_IsWidgetSoundBusyB
functions.summary: When battle flag +0x4244 is set, walks the party list (+0x4260) and returns 0 while an active member's actor is still busy (func_00669BAC / func_0066A2BC); else 1.

functions.name: Battle_QueueActionForGroupUnits
functions.summary: Battle action pass: iterates active units in four group unit lists (+0x4298, stride 0x1C) and queues action 0x54D via Battle_InsertActionSlot.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_CheckPartyStates
functions.summary: Consistency check over the battle party list at battle+0x4260: counts active members and verifies each against the manager's vtable+0x190 predicate, returning 0 on the first mismatch.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_AreUnitsIdleAndWindowIdle
functions.summary: Returns 1 when no battle unit in the 4x26 lists at +0x428C is active (vtable +0x18) and the window's own vtable +0x18C check is clear.

functions.name: Ui_CmdQueue_ProcessSlots2
functions.summary: Main per-frame processor of the UI command queue: walks every slot of the current frame, resolves the target window from the global list, checks its event state and executes or cancels the command, including the special ids at +0x88 and the 0x549 marker.

functions.name: Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry
functions.signature: void Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry(void * self, void * widget, int eventId, u32 stored, int slot, u8 mode)
functions.summary: Appends one entry to the battle command queue: stores the argument in the frame header, copies the widget into the frame slot, writes the event id and the mode byte and advances the frame index when slot 0 is used.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_IsWidgetSoundBusyC
functions.summary: Variant of 0x0016A2C8 that skips members in status 0x9A.

functions.name: Battle_ResetCommandQueue
functions.summary: Empties the battle command list (Battle_FreeCommandList walks the intrusive list at +0x110) and clears the queue-dirty byte at +0x13D.

functions.name: Battle_SyncUnitModelTransforms
functions.summary: Walks the four 26-entry battle-unit lists at world+0x428c and copies each live unit's model transform (+0x75c, three words) into the actor/model object registered for that unit id, keeping the rendered monsters and party models on top of their logical battle-unit positions.

functions.name: Battle_QueueUnitActions
functions.summary: Collects the actions already chosen by every battle unit (unit field +0xe94) and appends a battle action slot for each one, tagging it with the unit pointer and the manager's action counter before marking the source command as consumed (vtable+0xe4 with 0x5a).

functions.name: Battle_BuildTargetList
functions.signature: void Battle_BuildTargetList(BattleManager* self, BattleTarget* out, int count, int* outSideACount, int* outSideBCount)
functions.summary: Builds the candidate-target array for the current action: clears the caller's 8-byte entries, then enumerates the ally list (world+0x4254) and the enemy list (world+0x4270) into one id array. Each output entry receives the target id plus a flag saying whether it came from the first (ally) list.

functions.name: Field_Gimmick_CheckAllReady
functions.summary: Checks that all linked sub-objects in list self->f_110 have completed preparation by calling virtual method +0x2C on each.

functions.name: Battle_UpdateUnitCommandPhase
functions.summary: Advances one battle unit's command state machine: reads the unit's command byte (+0xBC), matches it against the four stored command slots (f_fd/f_100/f_103/f_106) and the literal states 3 and +0x40, clears the 3D balloon-pool flag at battleWork+0x4324 when the battle is in 3D mode, and finishes by setting the unit state through vtable+0x198 or vtable+0x14(9). Returns 0 for an unset (-1) or unknown command byte.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_ValidatePartyCommands
functions.summary: Validates every unit in the battle party list (battleWork+0x4260) and then commits the accepted ones: pass 1 requires all units to pass their vtable+0x10 predicate, pass 2 additionally requires the manager's +0x190 slot to accept them, pass 3 calls vtable+0x30(unit, 0, 1) on each accepted unit. Returns 1 when the party is ready and 0 otherwise; with an empty party it falls back to Battle_HasUnitInState1C.

functions.name: Field_Gimmick_TriggerEvent16
functions.summary: Dispatches event type 0x10 (16) to the gimmick controller state machine at +0xE4 with parameter value stored in field 0xFC.

functions.name: Battle_QueueDefaultActions
functions.summary: Fallback command pass: for every active party unit that is allowed to act (vtable +0x24), has no forced command (vtable +0x1C == 0) it appends the default action 0x2A to the action list through Battle_InsertActionSlot.

functions.name: Battle_RefreshEffectCommandList
functions.summary: 44-byte wrapper: fetches the battle work (work+8 -> +0x5C) and rebuilds its effect/command entry list through 0x00207DEC. Called from BattleScene_RefreshCommandWidgets.

functions.name: Battle_FinalizeUnitCommands
functions.summary: Second command pass over the party unit list (battle work +0x4260): builds each active unit's action descriptor with 0x00176948/0x001762AC and, for units that report a pending action (vtable +0x1C), commits it through vtable +0x50(unit, 1).

functions.name: Battle_SelectAiActions
functions.summary: Enemy AI turn: for every active battle unit it evaluates the unit's AI table (+0x8f0) against the current battle seed, rolls 1..100, chooses one of the unit's skill/attack ids, applies the skill's target/side rules, and appends the resulting action slots. This is the routine that decides what monsters do each round.

functions.name: Battle_DispatchUnitAction
functions.signature: void Battle_DispatchUnitAction(BattleManager* self, BattleUnit* unit, u32 actionId, int** outEntry)
functions.summary: Dispatches one unit's pending action: reads its category and sub-ids from +0xB0F7/+0xB0F9 (or the alternate block), invokes the matching handler from the manager's eleven-slot function table, and falls back to enqueuing generic action 0x14; finishes by calling the unit's vtable+0x48(1).

functions.name: Battle_RefreshUnitLineupEntries
functions.summary: Counts the present units in each of the four battle unit lists (battleWork+0x4298 + i*0x1C), stores the first unit's data id and the per-list count into the lineup fields (f_c4/f_cc/f_d4/f_dc and f_d0/f_d8/f_e0), then hands the assembled descriptor to the popup-entry builder 0x003FE054. Called from Battle_ResetLineupState.

functions.name: Battle_UpdatePhaseState
functions.summary: Derives the battle phase byte (+0xbc, values 0..8) from a series of virtual predicates on the manager (vtable+0x164..+0x188), so the main battle update can branch on a single state value.

functions.name: Container_DestroyList
functions.summary: Destroys a container: releases the owned object at +0xe4 and walks the intrusive list at +0x110, invoking each element's virtual destructor.

functions.name: Battle_FreeCommandList
functions.summary: Destroys every node of the manager's queued-command list (+0x110) through the node vtable slot +4. Called when a battle ends or the queue is rebuilt.

functions.name: Battle_BackupUnitActions
functions.signature: u32 Battle_BackupUnitActions(Battle * battle, ActionRecord * out, int slot, int actorId)
functions.summary: Snapshots the battle action table: copies all 80 action records (each holding five 0x8c-byte per-member sub-records) from the staging array to the backup array, clears the staging array, and copies the record belonging to actorId (optionally filtered by slot) into the caller's buffer.

functions.name: Battle_ExecuteItemAction
functions.signature: void Battle_ExecuteItemAction(BattleManager* self, uint32_t arg2, BattleAction* action)
functions.summary: Resolves a battle action that uses an item: reads the item id from the acting unit (vtable+0x84), looks up the item record, hands its id/effect data to the unit, then queues the item-use action (0xf) or its extended variant (0x10). The special item 0x120 (288) with world+0x4e64==0x45 forces a scan of the four unit lists for item 400, i.e. a scripted battle item event.

functions.name: Battle_CountActionTargets
functions.signature: int Battle_CountActionTargets(uint32_t arg1, int arg2, BattleUnit* action)
functions.summary: Counts how many candidates an action may hit: walks the ally container (world+0x4254) and the enemy container (world+0x4270), keeping units whose side matches the action's target mode (vtable+0xa8) and that report targetable (vtable+0x24). Returns the total count.

functions.name: Battle_Update
functions.summary: Main per-frame battle update: clears finished command objects, runs the queued action processing, executes the AI pass when this frame is not an interrupt, resolves the current action queue, updates the camera/scene hooks, and advances the phase/action counters. Also handles the 'battle over' hand-off to the next state.

functions.name: Battle_Start
functions.summary: Virtual battle-start entry: clears the current action slot, initialises the world battle interface, resets the action flags, syncs the unit model transforms, releases the previous battle scene object and calls the manager's vtable +0x2C to finish initialisation.

functions.name: Battle_Initialize
functions.summary: Battle initialisation used when the battle scene is created: same resets as Battle_Start, syncs unit transforms, hides the field view, releases the old battle scene object and calls the manager's vtable+0x2c. Called by the battle-scene setup routine 0x607B7C before its per-slot checks.

functions.name: Battle_UpdateActionQueue
functions.summary: Advances one battle action: asks the manager's virtual predicates whether an action is pending/ready, builds the action queue for the current unit (0x16BBF4) and the default/AI passes, and when the action completes marks the unit list dirty and starts the next action. Returns 0 (the caller keeps ticking).

functions.name: Battle_FindActiveUnit
functions.summary: Scans the manager's command/unit list (world+0x4260) and returns the first unit that is active, not dead and not suppressed, packaged into a small descriptor (0x176948/0x175F80/0x176134). Returns NULL when no unit qualifies. Used to pick 'whose turn is it'.

functions.name: Battle_ProcessUnitActions
functions.summary: Per-unit action pass for the ally-side unit list: for each live, non-suppressed unit it resolves the data id, dispatches the pending action (or the fallback action with the unit's category) and decrements the unit's remaining-action counter.

functions.name: Battle_QueueCommandByCategory
functions.summary: Queues the default command entry for a battle unit: lets the action object fill its six-byte descriptor, maps the unit's category byte (+0x31) to action id 0xE/2/3 in the auto-battle mode (work+0x4244) and otherwise uses id 1, then pushes or inserts the entry via Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry / Battle_InsertActionSlot according to the unit's +0xB0F7 flag.

functions.name: Battle_QueueAttackActions
functions.summary: Enqueues the two-step attack sequence for a unit: action 0xD (attack) followed by 0x2E (finish), appended through Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry or inserted through Battle_InsertActionSlot depending on the unit's +0xB0F7 mode, with the follow-up flag derived from the alive/state bytes.

functions.name: Battle_ResetUnitStates
functions.summary: Clears transient battle state on all units: empties the command list (calling each node's vtable+0x174/0x48 and 0x1CD53C), zeros the per-unit delay fields (+0x8e0/+0x8dc), and resets the four unit-group lists' animation/attack counters. Called between battles or on a full battle reset.

functions.name: Battle_InsertActionSlot
functions.signature: void Battle_InsertActionSlot(BattleManager* self, int index, BattleAction* action, uint32_t actionId, int arg5, uint8_t arg6)
functions.summary: Inserts one 0x2c8-byte action slot at the given index of the manager's 0x50-slot action array: first snapshots every slot into the backup array (+0xec), shifts the range [index..0x4e] up by one, zeroes the new slot, then hands the action descriptor to 0x3CDF74 which fills the slot and its five 0x8c sub-records.

functions.name: Battle_CheckActionSlotFree
functions.signature: u32 Battle_CheckActionSlotFree(Battle * battle, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
functions.summary: Checks whether the current unit's action slot is usable: validates each of the five per-member sub-records, and rejects the slot when the candidate actor id already appears in one of the record's ten target id fields.

functions.name: Battle_CountActionCandidates
functions.signature: int Battle_CountActionCandidates(uint32_t arg1, int arg2, BattleUnit* action)
