functions.name: maybe_Model_Actor_UpdateAttachmentVisibility
functions.summary: When the visibility result from the data table (0x0063DAD4 on f_3B0/f_3B4) differs from the cached byte f_31C, walks the attached parts at f_250 and shifts each part's f_304..f_318 block by the +/- constants at 0x00385D30/0x00385D34.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_Window_TickAndUpdateRandomIntervalTimer
functions.summary: 52-byte thunk: ticks the node's children (Field_SceneNode_TickChildren) and accumulates dt into self+0xBE, then falls through into the random-interval timer at 0x00385D6C (0x385D38 + 52 = 0x385D6C).

functions.name: maybe_Ui_Window_UpdateRandomIntervalTimer
functions.summary: Repeating random-interval timer: when f_B6 and f_58 are set it subtracts dt from the countdown f_BB and, on expiry, re-arms it to a random point in [f_B7,f_B8] (or [f_B9,f_BA] when byte +0x2D9 is set) plus 0.5 and calls the node's vtable +0x98.

functions.name: maybe_Field_Actor_SpawnEffectInstance
functions.summary: Initializes a field model actor and spawns attached effect instance from effect list using Container_KeyedList_SelectEntry.

functions.name: Field_Actor_SetIdleState
functions.summary: Sets the field actor to idle state: verifies motion state via 0x005E7818, and selects motion state 2 (if self->f_2F0 != 0) or state 0 via 0x005E7848.

functions.name: Field_Actor_SetWalkState
functions.summary: Sets the field actor to walking state: checks actor status via 0x005E78CC and activates animation motion state 3 via 0x005E74A0.

functions.name: Gfx_Actor_CreateFromConfig
functions.signature: void Gfx_Actor_CreateFromConfig(ModelActor* self, int kind, int* config)
functions.summary: Creates a field/battle model actor from a spawn record: copies the transform and appearance fields, builds the mesh, sets the animation state and attaches the sprite children for the transparent overlay pass.

functions.name: maybe_Field_Actor_ReleaseEffects
functions.summary: Release virtual of the field actor: while the actor is active it destroys the render node with Gfx_Node_Dtor and releases the actor's effect handle at +0x314 from the global handle table.

functions.name: Field_Gadget_TriggerCommand
functions.summary: Triggers the field gadget command 0x1A on the current field object.

functions.name: Battle_Ui_InitActionQueue
functions.signature: int Battle_Ui_InitActionQueue(u32 ctx, int descriptor, u32 queue, u32 initial)
functions.summary: Allocates and initializes the battle UI action queue: allocates buffer via 0x0028EF18, installs vtable g_003867D4 (0x007663C8+0xD4), and zeroes queue list pointers.

functions.name: Ui_Object_DtorWithChild
functions.summary: Deleting destructor for a UI object with one embedded child: installs the vtable, unlinks the list node, destroys the child and frees the object.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_DualDisplayWindow_SetMode
functions.signature: void maybe_Ui_DualDisplayWindow_SetMode(void* self, u32 mode, u32 arg3)
functions.summary: Mode setter: when arg3 is non-zero it switches on the mode argument and calls the matching dual-display mode selector (Ui_DualDisplayWindow_SelectMode for 0, 0x0045DB84 for 2, 0x0045DB38 for 3), then applies the resulting value through 0x001A6680 and a vtable call.

functions.name: Ui_TitleTextWindow_Open
functions.summary: Open step of the title-text window: drains queued input (0x0062F070/0x0010EBD8 until at most one entry remains), rebinds the list helper, selects the pane at self+0x918, assigns text id 0x1E to it and plays the open animation through the pane's slot +0x18.

functions.name: Ui_TitleTextWindow_InitPanesC
functions.summary: Window initialiser that delegates to func_0045E710 and then attaches only the 'txt_title' pane.

functions.name: Ui_Object_DtorWithArrayD
functions.summary: UI object destructor for an object owning three 0x330-byte records.

functions.name: Ui_FindObjectAtPosition
functions.signature: bool Ui_FindObjectAtPosition(FieldWork* scene, float* position, float radius)
functions.summary: Searches the field actor list for an object of the specific class (RTTI type 0x007C503C) whose +0x98/+0x9C coordinates lie within the query radius, returning whether such an object exists.

functions.name: Ui_ObjectList_End
functions.summary: Returns the end sentinel of the object list owned by the world manager (work+0x54, category 0) through func_001C7560, i.e. the terminator used by every list walk in this batch.

functions.name: Ui_ObjectList_Begin
functions.summary: Returns the head of the object list owned by the world manager (work+0x54, category 0) through func_001C7AD0 - the counterpart of 0x00386B0C.

functions.name: Ui_Actor_GetPortraitId
functions.summary: Resolves the portrait/face id (and two bytes) for the current actor from the character table.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_Actor_GetPortraitIdB
functions.summary: Second portrait-id query: resolves the portrait table entry for id 0 (0x0063EB94 + the actor portrait helper), maps the 0xFF miss to 0, and writes the byte id to out[0], the u16 style to out+2 and the size byte to out+4.

functions.name: maybe_Field_Placement_GetDefaultArea
functions.summary: Returns the placement area from 0x00423E94, or the compiled-in default descriptor 0x005A3630 when that returns 0. All three callers are field-placement tests, so the old 'Ui_GetDefaultValue' prefix was wrong.

functions.name: maybe_Model_Actor_UpdateScale
functions.summary: Re-applies the actor's model size from its f_78/f_7C dimensions and selects the visual scale: for overlay modes 1..4 it uses the fixed default scale constants, otherwise the Field2D visual state supplies the per-character scale and an update flag chooses between two globals.

functions.name: Model_Actor_UpdateScaleB
functions.summary: Second scale-setup path (no Field_SceneObject_SetModelSize call): for overlay modes 1..4 it assigns the fixed default scale to self+0x1D4 and the global at 0x00725374 to self+0x1CC; otherwise it applies the Field2D visual state for the current area/character, takes the character scale from VFP s0 into self+0x1D4 and picks one of the two global scales by Field2D_ShouldUpdateActorVisual.

functions.name: Battle_Ui_ResetSubPanels
functions.summary: Cleans up and resets all active sub-panels across the battle UI: checks active flags at offsets +0x154, +0x174, +0x608, +0x63C, and +0x6A4, invoking each sub-panel's virtual destructor +8 and clearing active flags.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_Row_SetItemIcon
functions.summary: Sets a row's item icon and label: resolves the item to a display model, stores the icon id at +0x138 and runs text command 5 or 6 (or 7 when the item is missing) so the row shows the icon/name; finally updates the attached text widget's width.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_ClearPendingInputB
functions.summary: Copy of 0x00382AD0: when Container_RingBuffer_Next reports another queued input event it clears the pending-input word at UiCore+0x94.

functions.name: Battle_Ui_TransitionState
functions.summary: Coordinates state transitions for battle UI panels: checks transition readiness, allocates node memory aligned to 0x10 bytes via 0x0011CFAC, resets existing sub-panels via 0x00386EC4, and activates new layout state.

functions.name: Ui_PartyList_BuildEntries
functions.summary: Builds the entry vector of a party/roster list window: links three intrusive list heads to their sentinels, binds the sub-objects at self+0x144, then walks the roster (Spirit_CountRosterEntries over the work+0x24A98 save block) and appends one 16-byte entry per member - index, id/name flag, selection match (Party_EntryMatchesSelectedId) and availability - through std_vector16_insert, finishing with Script_DispatchStateCallback.

functions.name: Ui_ScrollListWindow_Ctor
functions.summary: Constructor of the 0x12F0-byte scrolling list window: installs vtable 0x00766524, builds the embedded list widget through Ui_ListWidget_Ctor and the inline intrusive lists, then zeroes the per-row/scroll state.

functions.name: Ui_ScrollListWindow_Delete
functions.summary: Deleting destructor: runs the real destructor body then releases the object through the engine free.

functions.name: Ui_ScrollListWindow_Dtor
functions.summary: Complete destructor of the scrolling list window: unregisters the two renderer children, frees the list-view object, and unlinks the three intrusive node lists at +0x1298/+0x12B4/+0x12D0. First resets the object's vtable word to the base class vtable (g_00387C74), as ARMCC D1 destructors do.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_RecordWindow_CountByCategory
functions.summary: Recounts seen records for the window's category tabs: clears the twenty per-category counters at +0x24 and the total at +0xC4, walks the 590-row data-manager table, keeps rows whose bit is set in the seen bitset at work+0x2A2C8 and increments the counter indexed by the row's kind byte.

functions.name: Ui_RecordWindow_InsertSorted
functions.signature: void Ui_RecordWindow_InsertSorted(RecordWindow* self, u32 id, u32 value)
functions.summary: Inserts an (id, value) pair into the record window's sorted list unless the id is already flagged in the global seen-bitset, keeping the list ordered by id and value.

functions.name: Ui_RecordWindow_LoadEntriesChunk
functions.summary: Loads up to 30 record entries starting after the current index (or from 0 at the end), skipping ids already seen and inserting the rest into the sorted list with their display values.

functions.name: Battle_CommandQueue_Init
functions.summary: Allocates and initializes the 20-entry battle command ring buffer: calls 0x004712D0 to allocate buffer memory, configures circular list pointers at self+4, and zeroes 20 8-byte command slots.

functions.name: Battle_CommandQueue_Clear
functions.summary: Clears all pending commands from the battle command queue: walks the circular list from self[5] to self[4], frees allocated command payloads with 0x0010F6CC, and resets queue pointers.

functions.name: Fs_NamedObject_LoadSimple
functions.signature: void Fs_NamedObject_LoadSimple(u32 arg1, const char* name, u32 load, u32 arg4)
functions.summary: Loads (or finds) a named resource through the file-system named-object cache.

functions.name: Fs_NamedObject_LoadAndAdd
functions.signature: void Fs_NamedObject_LoadAndAdd(NamedObjectList* self, int index, u32 flags)
functions.summary: Loads a named object for one of the list records and inserts its handle into the handle vector, growing the vector when full and releasing evicted handles.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_Window_SetColorByState
functions.signature: void maybe_Ui_Window_SetColorByState(u32 handle, const char* record)
functions.summary: Applies a scene-state record to a packed UI resource: selects an FS transfer priority 0..4 from record bytes 3/4/0, releases the handle's 20 entries, and picks UI palette entry 7 or 4 by comparing the old and new state bytes.

functions.name: Container_ReleaseHandleVector
functions.summary: Releases every pack handle in the vector stored at self->f_108..f_10C (the vector for slot `slice`, 8 bytes per slot) and empties it by moving the end pointer back to the start.

functions.name: Battle_Ui_UpdatePartyRows
functions.summary: Per-unit battle UI update: loops all battle units and, for each non-null row object, drives the row (vtable+0x0C/+0x20), resolves the state variant from f_498..f_49E, plays or ends the row animation and copies the selected row's target into the unit's f_160->f_558.

functions.name: Battle_Ui_FlushPendingLogEntries
functions.summary: Flushes the per-slot battle-log messages: for every unit with a pending bit in obj+0x72C it releases the current layout, emits the queued popup entry for that slot's message id and clears the bit.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_Ui_InitActionSequenceEntries
functions.summary: Initialises the battle action-sequence entry list: copies a data-manager value into battle work +0x4324's f_250, then, by battle type (5, '$'=0x24 or others), appends sequence entries with random indices from the battle RNG and post-processes the ten type-5 slots.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_Ui_UpdatePartyLabels
functions.summary: For i < min(unit count, 5) it resolves the unit (slot 4 uses func_001F9B58 when self+0x168D is 1/3, otherwise self vtable+0x60; other slots use 0x002AB83C), finds the label object via the class hash table and calls maybe_Ui_Label_SetFromShortTriple(label, self + i*6 + 0x1404).

functions.name: maybe_Battle_Ui_UpdateStateMachine
functions.summary: Battle UI per-frame update: advances the unit-list/animation state, drains pending battle-log entries and spawns the queued multi-actor popups for the current battle state.

functions.name: Battle_ActorAnim_StepTimeline
functions.summary: Steps the battle actor animation timeline: iterates over active unit slots with stride 96 bytes, evaluates keyframe time delta, and triggers virtual animation update +0xFC on matching actor instances.

functions.name: Battle_Ui_InitSlots
functions.summary: One-time battle-UI slot setup: resets self+0x17EC0 to -1, initialises the party-window state (0x0020E48C, 0x002E7FB4), then for every unit chooses a slot variant from f_498..f_49E and the +0x1262/+0x1263/+0x1266/+0x1267 bytes and initialises each row's spell/skill list.

functions.name: FieldParty_CtorB
functions.summary: Constructor for the field party/companion display object that the field object factory spawns (kind 17). It installs the party vtable and constructs the two large per-member sub-objects (0x2EC7C bytes each) at +0x2208.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_Ui_UpdateStateMachineB
functions.summary: Tail block of the battle UI state machine: collects the per-slot values through the object's +0x48 virtual, spawns the multi-actor popup for them, updates unit transforms, then walks the two unit slots' update virtuals and writes the chosen stage id (0x1101..0x111B) through *out.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_Ui_UpdateCommandState
functions.summary: Battle UI step at state 0xD93: posts message 0x288, or 0x28E when action id self[0x48C] is 0x1A, then waits for the actor queue and a generation-tagged handle before advancing to 0xDA6.

functions.name: Battle_Ui_DeletingDtorA
functions.summary: Deleting destructor for battle UI object: calls base UI destructor 0x005F8528 and frees memory with 0x0010F6CC.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_Ui_UpdateCommandStateB
functions.summary: Battle UI step at state 0x991: posts message 0x48 (or 0x49 in the 3D/anchor branch), then waits for the actor queue and advances to 0x9A4.

functions.name: Battle_Ui_DeletingDtorB
functions.summary: Deleting destructor for secondary battle UI component: invokes 0x005F8528 and deallocates instance memory with 0x0010F6CC.

functions.name: Battle_ActorAction_Start
functions.summary: Initializes and starts a battle actor action: sets up subaction state machine, binds target actor pointers, and initiates action state.

functions.name: Battle_ActorAction_Update
functions.summary: Per-frame update of the battle actor action: evaluates action timing counters, processes subaction transitions, and updates actor transforms.

functions.name: Battle_ActorAction_Stop
functions.summary: Stops and concludes the battle actor action: resets active action parameters, halts subactions, and returns actor to idle state.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_ActionAnimObject_CtorA
functions.summary: Sub-object constructor for battle action animation: calls Battle_ActionSubObject_BaseCtor and installs vtable 0x00772274.

functions.name: Battle_ActorAction_DeletingDtor
functions.summary: Deleting destructor for Battle_ActorAction: calls base destructor 0x00193E44 and frees memory with 0x0010F6CC.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_Actor_UpdateIdleState
functions.summary: Battle actor-action timer: once the value returned by 0x00669D38 exceeds ~1.0 it resolves the actor by handle and replays its selected pose group, returning the actor to a stance after a second without action.

functions.name: Battle_ActorAction_Ctor
functions.summary: Tiny constructor of the battle actor-action sub-object: runs Battle_ActionSubObject_BaseCtor and installs the actor-action vtable (g_battleActorActionVtableB).

functions.name: Battle_ActorAction_WaitStart
functions.summary: Starts the wait/idle action state for a battle actor: configures wait timers and sets up idle animation parameters.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_ActionAnimObject_ClearSlotArray
functions.summary: Zeroes the 32 eight-byte slot records at base+0x480 (0x100 bytes) after the caller-supplied array construction; returns nothing.

functions.name: Battle_ActorAction_WaitUpdate
functions.summary: Per-frame update of the wait/idle action state for a battle actor: advances duration counters and checks for incoming action commands.

functions.name: Battle_Actor_MoveToPoint
functions.summary: Three-state move controller: state 0 interpolates the actor position from f_38/f_3C/f_40 towards f_44/f_48/f_4C by the f_54 progress (step g_0038AA08) and advances to state 2 at 1.0; state 2 plays the name g_0038AA10, snapshots the actor position and re-arms f_54; state 3 interpolates again towards f_30/f_34 with a different step, updating f_118.

functions.name: Battle_Actor_FinishMove
functions.summary: Ends a move action: resets the actor's action animation, and when the target actor is missing or not of the accepted types it snaps the actor position to the stored target (+0x2C..+0x34) and clears the ground clamp; finally rewinds the action to state 2.

functions.name: Ui_ListSubObject_Ctor_vt766910
functions.summary: Constructor of a list sub-object variant: runs the shared Ui_ListSubObject_BaseCtor and installs vtable 0x00766910 (plus the three-word default block from 0x007E7000 at +0x2C/+0x30/+0x44 and zeros at +0x50/+0x54).

functions.name: Battle_ActorAction_WaitDeletingDtor
functions.summary: Deleting destructor for battle actor wait action: invokes base destructor 0x00193E44 and frees memory with 0x0010F6CC.

functions.name: Battle_Action_RestoreActorIdleByHp
functions.summary: Restores a battle actor's post-action idle/injured posture based on current HP percentage: queries unit->vt[+0x90]/vt[+0x94] (HP/MaxHP), classifies HP% via 0x003CE464, and triggers critical/dead state vt[+0xE4](unit, 1, 1) when <=25% HP or normal idle clip 0 via 0x005E7848.

functions.name: Battle_Action_ResolveActor
functions.summary: Resolves and returns the battle actor owned by an action object, first from the active actor table and then from the reserve table; NULL when the owner is not currently a combatant.

functions.name: Ui_ListSubObject_BaseCtor
functions.signature: void* Ui_ListSubObject_BaseCtor(void* owner, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
functions.summary: Base constructor for list-row sub-objects: chains the list-row base constructor 0x00193D84, installs the derived vtable 0x0038AD20 and stores the owner at +0x28.

functions.name: Battle_ActorAction_DeletingDtorAlt
functions.summary: Deleting destructor for secondary battle actor action: invokes base destructor 0x00193E44 and deallocates memory via 0x0010F6CC.

functions.name: Ui_BattleEnemyListWindow_BuildRows
functions.summary: Fills the seven left/right text rows of the battle enemy list from the live battle actor tables: four party slots first, then every extra actor in the battle actor list, clamping each row to the actor's displayed name, level and colour. Rows beyond the number of live actors are hidden, and the selected party slot is marked.

functions.name: Ui_BattleEnemyListWindow_IsRowSelectable
functions.summary: Returns 1 when the row currently under the cursor can be selected: the row must exist, its actor must still be alive/visible, and (for a dead actor) the actor's death animation must have finished. Used by the cancel/confirm logic to keep the cursor off unusable rows.

functions.name: Ui_BattleEnemyListWindow_SkipInvalidCursor
functions.summary: Moves the list cursor forward until it lands on a selectable row, stepping over dead or hidden actors; if every remaining row is invalid it leaves the cursor where it is.

functions.name: Ui_BattleEnemyListWindow_OnRowSelected
functions.summary: Commits the row under the cursor: rebuilds the row display, writes the selected row index into the battle context highlight (+0x4210), resolves the actor, tells the actor which column/entry was chosen (vtable +0x64) and updates the command popup. Called when the player confirms a target.

functions.name: Ui_BattleEnemyListWindow_ClearSelection
functions.summary: Clears the battle context's target highlight (+0x4210 = 0xFF) and tells the currently bound actor that no row is selected, used when the window is closed or the target set is rebuilt.

functions.name: Ui_BattleEnemyListWindow_InitPanes
functions.summary: Builds the battle enemy-list window layout: seven left labels (txt_l1..txt_l7), seven right labels (txt_r1..txt_r7), seven null-text overlays sets the window columns, then creates the seven 'win_enemy_select%d' row frames and refreshes the row data.

functions.name: Ui_BattleEnemyListWindow_Ctor
functions.summary: Constructor for the battle enemy-list window: it installs the class vtable (dtor + InitPanes) and constructs seven 0x50-byte enemy rows at +0x70 that later hold one entry per on-screen enemy.

functions.name: Ui_BattleEnemyListWindow_Dtor
functions.summary: Deleting destructor of the battle enemy-list window: reinstalls the table, destroys the seven 0x50-byte child widgets at +0x1C, runs the UI base destructor and frees the window.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_SubWidgetConfig_Init
functions.summary: Creates the first sub-widget (0x194 bytes) and copies a large global layout template of rectangles, colours and flags into its fields (+0x18..+0xC0), constructing a 15-element 0x18-byte array. Called by Ui_InitFourSubWidgets, which builds four such sub-widgets.

functions.name: Battle_CommandWindow_Update
functions.summary: Per-frame update of the battle command window container: releases the active sub-window when it has finished, keeps the target-highlight byte in sync with the current actor, forwards the current pad/actor state to the selected sub-window (vtable +0x3C), then ticks all 29 registered sub-windows.

functions.name: Battle_CommandWindow_HandleResult
functions.signature: void Battle_CommandWindow_HandleResult(BattleCommandWindow* self, BattleCommandResult* result, BattleActor* actor)
functions.summary: Translates a sub-window result packet into the next battle-command state: codes 1/5 (confirm/cancel of the command page) and 2 (target page) drive the sub-window state machine, code 4 applies an equipment/skill action to the actor's slots, and everything else falls back to the idle state 0xD.

functions.name: Battle_CompareEquipPairStyle
functions.signature: int Battle_CompareEquipPairStyle(BattleActor* actor, int arg2, int mode, u32 itemId)
functions.summary: Compares the equipped-pair display style of a battle actor with the style of a supplied item (mode 0) or another item pair (mode 1): resolves the actor's member record and its two equipped item ids, classifies both with Item_ClassifyDualEquipCategory and returns non-zero when the styles differ.

functions.name: Battle_Command_GetTargetMode
functions.summary: Queries and caches the active target mode for the command: invokes virtual method +0x50 on target manager self->f_14 and stores the result in self->f_10.

functions.name: Battle_Command_OpenAttackTargetWindow
functions.summary: Opens the attack target selection window: calls virtual method +0x4C on battle window manager self->f_14 with window ID 9, configures display mode to 6, and shows the target selection UI.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_Command_OpenSubWindow
functions.summary: Opens battle command sub-window kind 3, resets its child and list, reads the selected unit's value (f_B0F6/f_B0F8 select f_B12C/f_B14C/f_B10C), fills the window with mode 4/2/5/6 depending on self->f_2C and finally calls vtable+0x78/+0x70.

functions.name: Battle_Command_AttachEquipToActor
functions.summary: Attaches equipment selected in the battle equip window to the active actor: hides sub-panel at self->f_C->f_C, unlinks old node via 0x0010EBE4, and attaches new equipment model node.

functions.name: Battle_Command_OpenItemPage
functions.summary: Opens battle command page 0x14 (hidden until the state machine selects it), runs that page's setup through Battle_ItemWindow_FillItemDetails and clears the UI result byte at self+0x41.

functions.name: Battle_ItemCommand_SetTargetMode
functions.summary: Configures target selection mode for the battle item command: sets window display mode to 3 (-1) via virtual method +0x60 on window self->f_10 and reveals target list via +0x70.

functions.name: Battle_Command_OpenItemWindow
functions.summary: Opens the battle item page (sub-window id 8) for the active actor: selects the item category from the actor's inventory record, sets the inventory colour/usable flags on the page and opens it with the item's id.

functions.name: Battle_Command_OpenSpellWindow
functions.summary: Opens the battle spell page (sub-window ids 7/6) for the active actor and pre-selects the actor's last-used spell from the actor's saved spell slot (+0x12E0/+0x12E2); the spell-list window then selects that entry.

functions.name: Battle_Command_OpenSkillWindow
functions.summary: Opens the battle skill (tokugi) page (sub-window ids 7/5) for the active actor and pre-selects the actor's last-used skill from actor+0x12DF/+0x12E1; the skill-list window then selects that entry.

functions.name: maybe_Battle_Command_OpenSpecialWindow
functions.summary: Opens battle command window kind 1, fills it (vtable+0x60(1,-1)), then either hides the child and calls the unit's vtable+0xBC, or shows it and passes the unit's f_B0F6/+0x2C3E bytes to 0x004AAC4C.

functions.name: Battle_Command_Update
functions.summary: Main per-frame state machine of the battle command page: publishes the current pad state to the active sub-window, waits for the actor to be ready, opens the attack page (id 1) on confirm, and dispatches the page result through the shared result handler.

functions.name: Battle_Command_OpenSpellTargetWindow
functions.summary: Opens the spell target selection window: calls virtual method +0x4C on manager self->f_14 with window type ID 0x11 (17) to instantiate the spell target window.

functions.name: Battle_Command_SetActorWindowEnabled
functions.signature: void Battle_Command_SetActorWindowEnabled(BattleCommandWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 scratch)
functions.summary: Shows or hides the actor's command sub-window depending on whether the actor currently has a valid command state (alive, not transformed, not in a special state). Called by every command-page update before it processes input.

functions.name: Battle_Command_OnInput
functions.signature: u32 Battle_Command_OnInput(BattleCommandWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 scratch)
functions.summary: Confirm/cancel input handler for a command page: cancel closes the page and raises the cancel SE when the current row is selectable, confirm returns the page's current selection to the command state machine.

functions.name: Battle_ItemCommand_Update
functions.summary: Item-page update: builds the item-use request for the selected inventory row, checks field/battle usability, and shows the 'cannot use here' or 'no target' battle popup before switching to the target page.

functions.name: Battle_ItemCommand_ExecuteAction
functions.summary: Dispatches the item action execution command: invokes virtual method +0x14 with command code 0xD (13) on the battle action dispatcher at *(self+8).

functions.name: Battle_ItemCommand_OnConfirm
functions.summary: Item-page confirm handler: validates that the chosen item can be used on the current actor/target, then either applies it directly or switches the page to the target-selection state.

functions.name: Battle_AttackTarget_Update
functions.summary: Attack-target page update: reads the selected enemy, refuses targets that are out of range or invalid, then either shows the 'out of range' popup or commits the attack action through the shared result handler.

functions.name: Battle_SpellTarget_Update
functions.summary: Spell-target page update: validates the chosen spell/target pair (range, target type, MP) and either opens the confirmation state or returns to the spell list with an error popup.

functions.name: Battle_Command_OpenSkillTargetWindow
functions.summary: Opens the skill target selection window: calls virtual method +0x4C on window manager self->f_14 with window ID 9 to open target selection for skills, then calls display methods +0x90 and +0x78.

functions.name: Battle_SkillTarget_Update
functions.summary: Ability-page update: dispatches on the chosen ability category (single ally, all allies, single enemy, all enemies, self, field) and validates range/MP before building the target commit packet.

functions.name: Battle_Command_UpdateSelection
functions.summary: Updates the currently highlighted selection in the active battle command window.

functions.name: Battle_Command_CommitActorAction
functions.signature: void Battle_Command_CommitActorAction(BattleCommandContainer* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 scratch)
functions.summary: Once the command state machine is finished, copies the chosen action/equipment selections into the actor's saved action slots, clears the pending-state flags and re-enables the actor's battle model update.

functions.name: Battle_Command_AdvanceState
functions.summary: Advances the battle command state machine from the current page to the next one (confirm -> target page, cancel -> equipment/previous page), based on the page result byte and the actor's pending flags.

functions.name: Ui_EquipListWindow_OpenForSlot
functions.summary: Opens the equipment-list sub-window (id 0x15) and points it at the saved slot: stores the window, sets its row count from the page object at +0x58, rebuilds the entries for the saved slot index and refreshes the cursor info text; with no saved slot it falls back to the container's own page switch instead.

functions.name: Battle_Equip_UpdateWeaponSlot
functions.summary: Equipment page update for the weapon slot: validates the selected weapon against the actor's equipment record, applies the weapon's stat/attack modifiers and switches the page to its confirmation state.

functions.name: Battle_Equip_UpdateArmourSlot
functions.summary: Equipment page update for the armour/accessory slot: validates the selected armour, updates the actor's defence/resistance block and either applies it or shows the 'cannot equip' popup.

functions.name: Battle_Command_OpenTacticsTargetWindow
functions.summary: Opens the tactics/strategy party member selection window: calls virtual method +0x4C on manager self->f_14 with window ID 0x11, storing window pointer in self->f_10 and revealing it via +0x78.

functions.name: Battle_Command_ExitState
functions.summary: Transitions out of the current battle command state: calls virtual method +0x4C on manager self->f_14 with window ID 0x11 to close the state window and reset self->f_10.

functions.name: Battle_Command_Cancel
functions.summary: Cancel handler for the battle command page: restores the previous command state, hides the command popup and returns the cursor to the previous page; when no page is open it falls back to the idle state.

functions.name: Battle_Command_CancelB
functions.summary: Second cancel path used when the command page is dismissed from the field/battle transition: closes the open page, restores the saved page and keeps the actor's pending command flags intact.

functions.name: Battle_CommandWindow_HideAll
functions.summary: Hides every battle command sub-window and clears the shared selection byte, used when the battle UI is torn down or the party member changes.

functions.name: Battle_CommandQueue_ReleaseSlots
functions.summary: Releases all active command slots in the battle command queue: checks 29 (0x1D) command entries at self[3], destroys allocated sub-object at self[2] via virtual destructor +4, and returns self.

functions.name: Ui_BattlePartyWindow_RenderRow
functions.signature: void Ui_BattlePartyWindow_RenderRow(BattlePartyWindow* self, u32 pane_base, u32 actor_id, int style)
functions.summary: Renders one party-status row: resolves the party member, picks its name/level/HP values, formats the HP and counter fields and writes the resulting strings into the five text panes of the row (pane_base..pane_base+4). Style 3 draws the two numeric columns (HP and MP) with separate formats.

functions.name: Battle_Item_CanTargetActor
functions.signature: int Battle_Item_CanTargetActor(BattleCommandWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 scratch)
functions.summary: Returns 0 when the actor bound to the item page is in a state that items cannot affect (dead, undead, or already at full effect), 1 otherwise. Used to grey out item targets.

functions.name: Ui_BattlePartyWindow_SyncCursor
functions.summary: Rebuilds the party window cursor: walks the four party slots, skips dead/absent members and members excluded by the current target filter, and moves the cursor to the matching row.

functions.name: Ui_BattlePartyWindow_InitPanes
functions.summary: Builds the four-row battle party status window: per member it creates the name label (txt_name1..4), the numeric level label (txt_num_l1..4), the HP label (txt_hp1..4), the two counter labels (txt_num_c/r) and a null-text overlay, plus the four 'win_enemy_select1..4' frames.

functions.name: Ui_BattlePartyWindow_RefreshRows
functions.summary: Refreshes the four party rows: shows/hides the row frames according to which party slots are present, re-renders each visible member's name/HP/counters, and restores the cursor to the previously selected member.

functions.name: Ui_BattlePartyWindow_Ctor
functions.summary: Constructor for the battle party-status window: installs the class vtable and constructs four 0x50-byte member rows at +0x70, one per party member shown in the battle HUD.

functions.name: Ui_BattleSpellWindow_DtorBase
functions.summary: Destructor body of the battle spell-list window: restores the spell-window vtable, destroys the four 0x50-byte sub-objects at +0x70 (list/scroll views), then runs the UI object base destructor and frees.

functions.name: Ui_BattleSpellWindow_Refresh
functions.summary: Rebuilds the battle spell list for the active actor: iterates the actor's learned spells (up to 0x28), writes each spell's name/cost/description into the list rows, applies the MP/availability colours and updates the scrollbar.

functions.name: Ui_BattleSpellWindow_HasSelectableSpell
functions.summary: Returns 1 when at least one actor in the battle still has a valid selectable spell slot for this window, 0 when every candidate is dead/disabled. Used to decide whether the spell tab can be opened.

functions.name: Ui_BattleSpellWindow_ClearSpellList
functions.summary: Empties the intrusive spell-entry list at +0x70, destroying every entry node through its virtual destructor and resetting the list head.

functions.name: Ui_BattleSpellWindow_SelectSpellEntry
functions.signature: void Ui_BattleSpellWindow_SelectSpellEntry(UiBattleSpellWindow* self, u32 spell_id, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
functions.summary: Finds the list row whose spell id matches and moves the window cursor to it, then tells the bound actor which spell is now highlighted. If the spell is absent the cursor is left unchanged.

functions.name: Ui_BattleSpellWindow_OnCursorMoved
functions.summary: Cursor-moved callback: tells the active battle actor which spell slot is now under the cursor so the 3D target preview updates.

functions.name: Ui_BattleSpellWindow_IsSpellUsable
functions.summary: Returns 1 when the currently highlighted spell can be cast by the actor (enough MP, not silenced, target exists); used to block confirm on greyed-out rows.

functions.name: Ui_BattleSpellWindow_BuildSpellList
functions.summary: Builds the sorted spell-entry list for the active actor: allocates one 0x10-byte node per learned spell, stores its id and sort key (spell level), inserts the nodes ordered by key and refreshes the list view.

functions.name: Ui_Window_ToggleDisplayStateA
functions.summary: Toggles the window display state: queries display configuration parameters from template g_00392094 based on show_flag, calls virtual method +0x4C to set layout dimensions, and updates visibility via virtual method +0x40.

functions.name: Ui_ThreeRowTextWindow_Delete
functions.summary: Deleting destructor of the three-row text window: frees the font/layout resource at +0x84, releases the handle at +0x88 and clears the flag word, then frees the widget.

functions.name: Ui_ThreeRowTextWindow_InitPanes
functions.summary: Creates a header-plus-three-row text window: txt_l1..l3 / txt_r1..r3 plus a center 'txt_text' label and the null-text overlays.

functions.name: Battle_TextLayout_Ctor
functions.summary: Constructor of the battle text-layout object: allocates the UI object, creates its intrusive list heads, loads 'battle_Text.bxon' through the pack manager and keeps a handle to the first parsed text resource.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_Panel_Delete
functions.summary: Out-of-line release+delete of a panel: stores the passed vtable, releases the pack handle at +0x88, unlinks the child list, destroys the child with the base destructor and frees the panel.

functions.name: Battle_TextLayout_RefreshPartyList
functions.summary: Rebuilds the per-party-member text rows used by the battle command UI: for each of the four party slots it reads the member's name, level and status and writes them into the layout's text panes, hiding empty slots.

functions.name: Ui_BattleSkillWindow_ClearSkillList
functions.summary: Empties the intrusive skill-entry list at +0x70, destroying every node through its virtual destructor and resetting the list head.

functions.name: Ui_BattleSkillWindow_SelectSkillEntry
functions.summary: Moves the skill-list cursor to the row with the given skill id, accounting for the window's multi-column layout (group index at +0x64), and updates the list selection.

functions.name: Ui_BattleSkillWindow_OnCursorMoved
functions.summary: Cursor-moved callback for the skill list: forwards the highlighted skill slot to the active actor so the battle preview follows the cursor.

functions.name: Ui_BattleSkillWindow_BuildSkillList
functions.summary: Builds the sorted skill-entry list for the active actor: allocates one 0x10-byte node per learned skill, stores id + sort key, inserts it in order and refreshes the grid view.

functions.name: Ui_Window_ToggleDisplayStateB
functions.signature: void Ui_Window_ToggleDisplayStateB(int* self, int show_flag, u32 auxiliary, u32 transition)
functions.summary: Toggles secondary window display state: applies visibility flag through virtual method +0x40 and updates window geometry via +0x4C using parameters from template g_00392DA8.

functions.name: Ui_BattleSkillWindow_DeleteList
functions.summary: Deleting helper for the battle skill window: releases the skill list, resets the column index and runs the base list cleanup.

functions.name: Ui_FourRowTextWindow_InitPanes_2
functions.summary: Creates a four-row, two-column text window: txt_l1..l4 and txt_r1..r4 with matching null-text overlays.

functions.name: Ui_NextBattleIcon_Update
functions.signature: void Ui_NextBattleIcon_Update(UiNextBattleIcon* self, u32 arg2, BattleSprite* sprite, u32 icon)
functions.summary: Resolves the 'icon_next_battle_3d' or 'icon_next_battle_2d' pane depending on the current render mode and attaches its texture to the supplied battle sprite actor.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_EntryListWindow_Ctor
functions.summary: Constructor of a small list-owning window: window base, vtable 0x00766B74, sentinel byte +0x6E = 0xFF and one intrusive list head at +0x70 initialised to empty (three self-pointers, zero count).

functions.name: Ui_FourRowTextWindow_DeletingDtor
functions.summary: Deleting destructor of the battle four-row text window: re-splices the two intrusive lists at +0x74/+0x78, runs Ui_Object_DtorBase and frees.

functions.name: Ui_ToggleChildVisible
functions.summary: Applies the inverse of the `hide` flag to the child pane at +0x70: runs the widget update bookkeeping (0x0032570C) and then sets the pane visibility to !hide.

functions.name: Ui_TextLayerWindow_Init
functions.signature: void Ui_TextLayerWindow_Init(UiWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
functions.summary: Window initialiser whose whole job is to give the dual-layer text renderer embedded at self+0x70 its default setup (Text_SetupDualLayersDefault), after the shared UI base constructor.

functions.name: Ui_MessageTextRenderer_Init
functions.summary: Creates the message-window text renderer: allocates it via the message-window base and installs the dual-layer text vtable at +0x70.

functions.name: Ui_TextLayerWindow_DeletingDtor
functions.summary: Secondary-base deleting destructor of the text-layer window: adjusts this by -0x70 (multiple inheritance), runs Ui_Object_DtorBase on the primary base and frees. The primary object carries the text-layer setup.

functions.name: Ui_NumberedTextRowsWindow_InitPanesB
functions.summary: Variant of the three-row numbered text window: builds three rows from 'null_txt_l1' with an incrementing digit, registering each through virtual +0x34/+0x38 and finishing with +0x48.

functions.name: Ui_NumberedTextRowsWindow_DeletingDtor
functions.summary: Deleting destructor (slot 0) of the numbered-text-rows window: runs Ui_Object_DtorBase and frees; it owns no extra arrays.

functions.name: Casino_Slot_StopAllReels
functions.summary: Stops (or leaves running) all six slot reels: stores the stop flag and, when stopping, asks each of the six reel plates to end its spin animation.

functions.name: Ui_SlotMachineDisplay_Dtor
functions.summary: Destructor of the casino slot-machine display part: calls the release hook stored at +0x98, tears down the reel container at +0x120 and releases the six reel/animation elements at +0xEC0, +0x1064, +0x1208, +0x13AC, +0x1550, +0x16F4.

functions.name: Casino_Slot_HideSymbols
functions.summary: Hides symbol slots 3, 4 and 5 on every one of the six reels (the symbols that are only shown while spinning).

functions.name: Ui_Frame_SetColorVariant
functions.summary: Updates the color variant of a UI window frame: looks up child panes 'frame_green', 'frame_blue', and 'frame_red' via virtual method +0x2C on self->f_A8, and toggles visibility bit 0 at +0x44 to match the selected color variant.

functions.name: Ui_Frame_UpdateBorderTiles
functions.summary: Updates the 9-slice border tiles and corner sprites for the UI frame: iterates across 6 border segments at self+0x78 (stride 6), dispatching tile setup calls 0x004C2DD8 and 0x004C2FDC.

functions.name: Ui_Window_DispatchLayoutDraw
functions.signature: void Ui_Window_DispatchLayoutDraw(int self, int render_ctx, int* target_ctx)
functions.summary: Dispatches layout draw commands for child window elements: sets target context slot 0x183 to render_ctx+4, and calls virtual draw method +0x24 when self+0x98 is valid.

functions.name: Ui_SlotMachine_Ctor
functions.summary: The casino slot-machine constructor: it installs the vtable and builds the reel/lamp chain (0x4AD8B4, 0x4EFAC8 and six 0x4C37D4 elements).

functions.name: Ui_Frame_DeletingDtor
functions.summary: Deleting destructor for UI frame object: tears down frame sub-components via 0x004C391C, 0x001D8C2C, and 0x004AD9B8, then frees memory with 0x0010F6CC.

functions.name: Casino_Slot_InitPanes
functions.summary: Builds the slot-machine window layout: five belt rows, fifty reel-symbol frames, the two side lamps, the queen-select row, the three animation layers (freespin, metalchange, queen) and the 'menu_casino_jackpot' effect object.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_UpdateElementArray5
functions.summary: Updates the five slot-window element records at self+0x5c0 (stride 0x238) by calling the per-element update routine on each; the caller is the slot window's pattern processor, so these are the five payline/hit indicators.

functions.name: Casino_Slot_ReleaseEffects
functions.summary: Releases the slot machine's animated jackpot object at +0x1544 and the embedded effect handle at +0x98.

functions.name: Casino_Slot_ResetRows
functions.summary: Clears the five slot-machine row objects at self+0x5C0 (stride 0x238) through Ui_HitIcon_ClearAllSlots, resetting the hit-icon state of every payout row.

functions.name: Ui_Dialog_UpdateLayout
functions.summary: Updates dialog layout panes and text alignment: checks dialog dimensions, recalculates line rects, and triggers pane layout sync.

functions.name: Casino_Slot_SetThreeDigits
functions.summary: Writes a three-digit number to a slot-machine plate: each of the three digit objects shows value+2, value+1 and value.

functions.name: Casino_Slot_ApplyRowState
functions.summary: Resets the slot machine's five reel rows and then creates their icon sprites for one display state: Ui_HitIcon_ClearAllSlots on each of the five 0x238-byte rows at +0x5C0, then Ui_HitIcon_CreateSprites(row, index, state).

functions.name: Casino_Slot_RenderReels
functions.signature: void Casino_Slot_RenderReels(CasinoSlot* self, u32* drawBuffer, UiRenderContext* ctx, SceneNode* node)
functions.summary: Emits the frame's draw commands for the five slot reels: it appends the 'background' and 'side_lamp_bottom' panes, then for each reel either hides it (alpha 0xFF) when it has not started spinning or draws its two symbol quads with alpha 0xA0, finally restoring the two decorative panes to visible.

functions.name: Casino_Slot_Ctor
functions.summary: Constructor for the slot-machine object itself: installs the Casino_Slot vtable, builds its counter/effect/widget sub-objects and then constructs the five 0x238-byte reel objects that Casino_Slot_RenderReels draws.

functions.name: Casino_Slot_Dtor
functions.summary: Complete destructor of the casino slot-machine window: destroys the five payout rows (0x238 stride), the three 0x54-byte side widgets, the five 0x50-byte belt widgets, the 0x18*0x10 symbol grid and the two child objects before freeing.

functions.name: Ui_SaveIconWindow_Init
functions.summary: Creates and attaches the 'win_save_icon' pane for the save/suspend icon and starts it hidden, ready for the save routine to show.

functions.name: Ui_TitleMessageWindow_Close
functions.summary: Close handler of the title message window: hides the two renderer layers (the UI context's layer objects at +0x1C and +0x10), then releases the message page attached at +0x11C.

functions.name: Ui_TitleMessageWindow_Update
functions.summary: Per-frame update of the title message window: advances the anim sequence and the cursor repeat timer, accumulates the frame delta, and dispatches the current sub-page handler from the inline page table at +0x11C (five 0x18-byte entries).

functions.name: maybe_Ui_SaveIcon_Update
functions.summary: Save-icon update; the readable body is empty because Ghidra dropped the control flow, so only the return value survives.

functions.name: Ui_Dialog_SetVisibleState
functions.summary: Sets dialog visibility state and triggers show/hide transitions on the active dialog panes.

functions.name: Ui_Dialog_ResetAnimation
functions.summary: Resets opening and closing animation timelines for the UI dialog to baseline state.

functions.name: Ui_Window_WaitForAnimA
functions.summary: Waits for the window's layout animation to finish: ticks the animation player at self+0x1c8 and, once it is done, fires the window's finish callback at +0x11C.

functions.name: Ui_Window_WaitForAnimB
functions.summary: Second animation-wait variant: ticks the same layout player and invokes the finish callback when the animation has completed; used by windows whose player is started by their enter hook.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_Dialog_SelectPage
functions.summary: Dialog command handler: sets the page-state object at +0x1C0, drains its page queue, resolves the current page pointer from the record (clamped to the record count) and rebinds +0x1C8, then enables the panel at +0x1F0C.

functions.name: Ui_Window_WaitForAnimC
functions.summary: Third animation-wait variant: waits for both the layout player and the screen-flow timer (f_124 > 0x3FFFFFFF), then fires the finish callback at +0x11C.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_Window_HandleConfirmCancel
functions.summary: Once the mode transition at self+0x1C0 has finished, picks a state from the flags word at self+0x1C4 - 1 when bit 0x20 or 0x40 is set, 2 when bit 2 is set, 4 otherwise - and commits the request through the state machine at self+0x11C.

functions.name: Ui_TitleMessageWindow_Ctor
functions.summary: Constructor for the title-screen message/confirm window. It installs the TitleMessage window vtable and creates the embedded member-pair child plus five 0x18-byte sub-elements used by the window's layout rows.

functions.name: Ui_Dialog_DeletingDtor
functions.summary: Deleting destructor for UI dialog: calls base destructor and deallocates memory with 0x0010F6CC.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ReleaseChildren
functions.summary: Release/teardown helper of a large message-style window: stores the class vtable, drops the handles at +0x2078/+0x207C and walks the child chain at +0x20D0 releasing message pages, two text elements, a panel and the animation object.

functions.name: Ui_Dialog_ProcessInput
functions.summary: Processes controller input for the active UI dialog: evaluates directional pad navigation, A/B button confirmations/cancellations, and updates selection cursor.

functions.name: Ui_TextWindow_AdvanceLine
functions.summary: When the window is in one of the four active message states (2..5), emits the next control byte of the current line buffer through Ui_MessageWindow_ExecNextControlByte and stores the resulting cursor pair.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_TextWindow_RefreshLine
functions.summary: Refreshes the current line: in an active message state it emits the next control byte when the read and write cursors (f_1948/f_194C) differ, otherwise it clears the line with the empty string.

functions.name: Ui_Dialog_UpdateChildren
functions.summary: Per-frame update of child dialog widgets, text panes, and scrolling indicators.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ShowNextPageWithControls
functions.summary: Shows the next page of a message: releases the current page elements, emits the control codes 0x2E..0x3B that build the page header/footer and then pushes the first control byte of the page.

functions.name: Ui_MessageWindow_ExecNextControlByte
functions.summary: Reads the next byte from a message cursor and executes it as a control code, passing the 'last byte of the line' flag so the renderer knows when the line ends.

functions.name: Cutscene_LoadScenarioPacks
functions.summary: Loads every scenario pack referenced by the current cutscene: builds the '3d/cs/scenario/%s/%s.pack' name for each entry, opens it through the pack manager and grows the scene's pack-handle array as needed.

functions.name: Cutscene_ApplyLayoutMode
functions.summary: Applies the cutscene's 2D/3D layout mode: switches the render layer used for the scene (0/1/2), configures the camera and the message layer, and restores the scene's UI state when the cutscene ends.

functions.name: Cutscene_AttachMantleToActor
functions.summary: Attaches the 'cbhm_tcs_mant' (cutscene mantle/cloak) model attachment to the actor currently being animated by the cutscene.

functions.name: Cutscene_OpenMessageForActor
functions.signature: void Cutscene_OpenMessageForActor(CutsceneScene* self, u32 actor_handle, u32 text_id, u32 speaker_id, int mode, ...)
functions.summary: Prepares and opens the cutscene message window for an actor: resolves the actor's model, applies the face/expression state, chooses the display token and calls the message window with the formatted string.

functions.name: Ui_MessageWindow_CloseActive
functions.summary: Closes whatever message window is currently active: reads the message object from the UI layer (+0x98), calls Ui_MessageWindow_Close and then hides its text. This is the script-facing 'MessageEnd'-style helper.

functions.name: Cutscene_ApplyLayerFlags
functions.summary: Applies the cutscene's per-layer visibility flags to the render layer object: converts the scene's flag byte at +0x16 into the renderer's 0/1/2/4/8 mask so the correct 3D or 2D layer is drawn during the cutscene.

functions.name: Cutscene_Finish
functions.signature: u32 Cutscene_Finish(CutsceneScene* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
functions.summary: Finishes the current cutscene: restores the normal render output, marks the renderer as dirty (+0x35) and releases the scene camera/effect object at +0x14C.

functions.name: Cutscene_ResolveActorResource
functions.summary: Resolves the resource object for the cutscene's current actor: looks the handle up in the scene resource list, falls back to the shared render resource and caches the result at +0x20/+0x2C.

functions.name: Cutscene_FindResourceEntry
functions.signature: int Cutscene_FindResourceEntry(CutsceneScene* self, int index, u32 handle, int* out_a, int* out_b)
functions.summary: Looks up one cutscene resource slot and returns 1 when both the primary and secondary resource objects for the handle exist.

functions.name: Ui_Dialog_Render
functions.summary: Draws the dialog frame, background, text, and active buttons to the current UI render target.

functions.name: ds9
functions.signature: u32 ds9(int arg1, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int arg4, u32 arg5, int * arg6)

functions.name: Script_LookupIntTableValue
functions.signature: u32 Script_LookupIntTableValue(ScriptContext* self, u32 packetId, u32 arg3, int index, u32 key, int* out)
functions.summary: Resolves an integer table entry for a script: tries the packet/actor table first, then the context's own int table (Script_GetIntTable3) and finally the per-slot table, writing the value to *out and returning 1 on success.

functions.name: Model_LookupEntryValue
functions.signature: u32 Model_LookupEntryValue(ModelContext* ctx, u32 packetId, u32 arg3, int index, u32 key, int* out)
functions.summary: Three-stage value lookup by key: first the model record reached through packetId (record+0x160 -> +0x11c -> Model_FindEntryById), then the context's own resource descriptor, then the descriptor in the ctx+0x30 table at the given index; writes the first non-zero result to *out and returns 1, or returns 0.

functions.name: lZd
functions.signature: void lZd(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

functions.name: Cutscene_ReleaseMessageAndCamera
functions.summary: Releases the cutscene's message-window and camera objects and drops the cached camera animation handle at +0x148 when the scene closes.

functions.name: Cutscene_Init
functions.summary: Initialises a cutscene scene from its descriptor: stores the scene id/layout/flags, resolves the scene resource handle, sets up the default camera and prepares the pack that will hold the scene's assets.

functions.name: Cutscene_Close
functions.summary: Closes the cutscene: stops the camera and message animations, releases the cached camera-animation handle and clears the scene's pending display object.

functions.name: Cutscene_UpdateTimer
functions.summary: Advances the cutscene's frame timer and, when the current scene step ends, loads the next scene resource or shuts the scene down. Also feeds the current scene id into the message/sound systems.

functions.name: Script_TCSJump_Check
functions.summary: Implements the validation half of the TCSJump native: resolves the scene frame, checks the TCS scene/table state and the frame index, seeks the scene and returns 1 when the jump is valid.

functions.name: Cutscene_Teardown
functions.summary: Tears down a cutscene scene: releases the camera/effect object, destroys every pack handle in the 8-byte vector, releases the text resource and resets all scene fields to their empty values.

functions.name: Cutscene_CreateActorModels
functions.signature: void Cutscene_CreateActorModels(CutsceneScene* self, u32 scene, u32 actor_id, int face_id, int expression, ...)
functions.summary: Creates the visible models for a cutscene actor: resolves the actor's model definition, applies face/expression overrides and attaches the model to the scene's actor slot.

functions.name: Script_TCS_FindSceneFrame
functions.summary: Finds a named entry in the current TCS scene table (0xC-stride entries under self->f_2C->f_60) and returns its index, or 0xFFFFFFFF when absent.

functions.name: Cutscene_AdvanceTimeline
functions.summary: Advances the cutscene timeline by one slot: consumes the next scene event/handle, updates the actor/camera attachments and triggers the scene's follow-up step when the slot count is exhausted.

functions.name: Cutscene_Scene_Init
functions.summary: In-place initialiser for a cutscene scene: stamps both of its vtable bases (scene interface and a second render/timeline interface), links the owning object, clears the scene's flags/list heads and copies the default 12-float transform/timing table. Called when the field scene objects are set up.

functions.name: Cutscene_Scene_Dtor
functions.summary: Destructor of the cutscene scene: runs the full teardown, releases the camera handle at +0x14C, destroys the two 0x14-byte vectors and frees the object.

functions.name: Ui_PanelState_ResetProperties
functions.summary: Clears all layout property fields on the panel state object: zeroes 11 consecutive short values from self+0xC to self+0x20, and resets flags self->f_5A and self->f_5B.

functions.name: Ui_PanelState_InitProperties
functions.summary: Initializes property arrays for the UI panel state: clears 32 (0x20) property slots of 8 bytes each using default property descriptor uRam003989F8.

functions.name: Ui_TextLineCache_Init
functions.summary: Clears the three 0x180-byte text-line buffers and their counters/flags (+0x480..+0x495); the callers allocate this as a stack temporary before composing multi-line message text.

functions.name: Ui_TextLineCache_InitAndReturn
functions.summary: Initializes a 0x496-byte Ui_TextLineCache by zeroing its three 0x180-byte line buffers (+0x000, +0x180, +0x300) and metadata fields (+0x480..+0x495), then returns self.

functions.name: Ui_DungeonListWindow_Delete
functions.summary: Deleting destructor of the dungeon-list window: stamps its vtable, releases the layout at +0x4C and the child list, then frees.

functions.name: Ui_DungeonListWindow_Init
functions.summary: Initialises the dungeon-list window: attaches the 'win_dungeon_list2' pane, links the embedded list headers at +0x18C/+0x17C and refreshes the list.

functions.name: Field_NpcAction_TurnTowardActorStart
functions.signature: void Field_NpcAction_TurnTowardActorStart(FieldNpcAction* self, u32 action, int target)

functions.name: Field_NpcAction_TurnTowardActorUpdate
functions.summary: Per-frame update of the NPC turn-toward-actor action: evaluates orientation difference via (*self->f_98->f_2C)(), accumulates rotation time delta g_00398D1C into self->f_128, and updates rotation states.

functions.name: Field_NpcAction_TurnTowardActorEnd
functions.summary: Concludes the NPC turn-toward-actor action: restores default actor visibility and interaction flags via 0x0029126C.

functions.name: maybe_Ui_DungeonList_CanClose
